lessons.title: Roman Numbers: Writing Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Roman numbers

We use Roman numbers with symbols I = 1, V = 5 and X = 10. Our normal numbers like 3, 7 and 15 are called Hindi-Arabic numbers.

1 = I, 2 = II, 3 = III, 5 = V, 10 = X, 15 = XV, 20 = XX

When a smaller symbol comes after a bigger symbol, we add it: VI = 5 + 1 = 6 and VIII = 5 + 3 = 8. When I comes before V or X, we subtract it: IV = 5 - 1 = 4 and IX = 10 - 1 = 9.

Worked example

Write 14 in Roman numbers.

Step 1: Split 14 as 10 + 4.

Step 2: 10 is X and 4 is IV.

Step 3: Join them: X + IV = XIV.

Answer: 14 = XIV. In the same way 16 = XVI, 17 = XVII and 19 = XIX.

Key points

  • I = 1, V = 5, X = 10.
  • Add when a small symbol is after a big symbol.
  • Subtract for IV = 4 and IX = 9.

mcqs.q: What is 5 in Roman numbers?
mcqs.why: 5 is a basic Roman symbol. In the exercise, 5 is written as V.

mcqs.q: What is 7 in Roman numbers?
mcqs.why: Split 7 as 5 + 1 + 1. 5 is V and 1 + 1 is II, so 7 = V + II = VII.

mcqs.q: What is 11 in Roman numbers?
mcqs.why: Split 11 as 10 + 1. 10 is X and 1 is I, so 11 = X + I = XI.

mcqs.q: What is 9 in Roman numbers?
mcqs.why: 9 is one less than 10, so write I before X. 10 - 1 = 9, so 9 = IX.

mcqs.q: What is III in Hindi-Arabic numbers?
mcqs.why: III means 1 + 1 + 1. Adding them gives 1 + 1 + 1 = 3, so III = 3.

mcqs.q: What is IV in Hindi-Arabic numbers?
mcqs.why: I before V means one less than 5. So IV = 5 - 1 = 4.

mcqs.q: What is XV in Hindi-Arabic numbers?
mcqs.why: XV means 10 + 5. Adding them gives 10 + 5 = 15, so XV = 15.

mcqs.q: What is XIX in Hindi-Arabic numbers?
mcqs.why: XIX means 10 + 9. Adding them gives 10 + 9 = 19, so XIX = 19.

mcqs.q: Which number comes after I in: I, __, III?
mcqs.why: Count in order: I is 1, then 2, then III is 3. So the missing number 2 is II.

mcqs.q: What is 20 in Roman numbers?
mcqs.why: Split 20 as 10 + 10. Write X two times, so 20 = XX.

lessons.title: Roman Numbers: More Practice
lessons.notes_html:
Clocks and matching

A clock face shows Roman numbers from I to XII in order. To find a missing clock number, count I, II, III, IV, V, VI, VII, VIII, IX, X, XI, XII and see which ones are not shown.

Clock (a) shows XI, I, III, V, VI and IX, so the missing numbers are II, IV, VII, VIII, X and XII.

Worked example

Match XII with its Hindi-Arabic number.

Step 1: Split XII as 10 + 1 + 1.

Step 2: Add: 10 + 1 + 1 = 12.

Answer: XII matches 12. Also V matches 5, IX matches 9, VII matches 7 and II matches 2.

Roman numbers 1 to 20

1 = I, 2 = II, 3 = III, 4 = IV, 5 = V, 6 = VI, 7 = VII, 8 = VIII, 9 = IX, 10 = X, 11 = XI, 12 = XII, 13 = XIII, 14 = XIV, 15 = XV, 16 = XVI, 17 = XVII, 18 = XVIII, 19 = XIX, 20 = XX.

Key points

  • Clocks use I to XII.
  • Read Roman numbers by adding, except IV and IX.
  • Learn the full list from 1 to 20.

mcqs.q: A clock shows XI, I, III, V, VI and IX. Which number is missing?
mcqs.why: Count I to XII in order. VII is 7 and it is not in the shown list, so VII is missing.

mcqs.q: What does V match?
mcqs.why: V is a basic Roman symbol for 5, so in the matching exercise V matches 5.

mcqs.q: What does IX match?
mcqs.why: IX means one less than 10. So IX = 10 - 1 = 9, and IX matches 9.

mcqs.q: What does VII match?
mcqs.why: VII means 5 + 1 + 1. Adding gives 5 + 2 = 7, so VII matches 7.

mcqs.q: What does VIII match?
mcqs.why: VIII means 5 + 1 + 1 + 1. Adding gives 5 + 3 = 8, so VIII matches 8.

mcqs.q: What is 13 in Roman numbers?
mcqs.why: Split 13 as 10 + 3. 10 is X and 3 is III, so 13 = X + III = XIII.

mcqs.q: What is 18 in Roman numbers?
mcqs.why: Split 18 as 10 + 5 + 3. That is X + V + III, so 18 = XVIII.

mcqs.q: Clock (b) shows XII, X, II, VIII, IV and VI. Which number is missing?
mcqs.why: Count I to XII in order. I is 1 and it is not in the shown list, so I is missing.

mcqs.q: What does XI match?
mcqs.why: XI means 10 + 1. Adding gives 10 + 1 = 11, so XI matches 11.

mcqs.q: What is 14 in Roman numbers?
mcqs.why: Split 14 as 10 + 4. 10 is X and 4 is IV, so 14 = X + IV = XIV.

lessons.title: Even and Odd Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Even and odd numbers

Even numbers have 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8 at the ones place. Odd numbers have 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9 at the ones place. Only look at the last digit.

From 80, 83, 15, 98, 67, 78, 42, 27, 45, the even numbers are 80, 98, 78 and 42. From 30, 38, 71, 32, 64, 69, 70, 11, 95, the odd numbers are 71, 69, 11 and 95.

Worked example

Is 23 an even number? True or false?

Step 1: Look at the ones place of 23, which is 3.

Step 2: 3 is an odd digit, so 23 is odd.

Answer: False. 23 is an odd number. But 30 is even and 15 is odd, so both those statements are true.

Key points

  • Even numbers go 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and keep adding 2.
  • Odd numbers go 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and keep adding 2.
  • After 30, the first five even numbers are 32, 34, 36, 38, 40.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an even number?
mcqs.why: Look at the ones place. 98 ends in 8, and 8 is an even digit, so 98 is even.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an odd number?
mcqs.why: Look at the ones place. 71 ends in 1, and 1 is an odd digit, so 71 is odd.

mcqs.q: What are the even numbers between 1 and 20? The list starts 2, 4, 6, __. What comes next?
mcqs.why: Even numbers keep adding 2: 2, 4, 6, then 6 + 2 = 8, so 8 comes next.

mcqs.q: After 30, what is the first even number?
mcqs.why: 30 is even, so the next even number is 30 + 2 = 32. It is the first even number after 30.

mcqs.q: After 50, what is the first odd number?
mcqs.why: 50 is even, so the next number 51 ends in 1 and is odd. The first odd number after 50 is 51.

mcqs.q: True or false: 52 is an odd number.
mcqs.why: Look at the ones place of 52, which is 2. 2 is an even digit, so 52 is even, not odd. The statement is false.

mcqs.q: Which number is even: 15, 27, 42 or 95?
mcqs.why: Check the ones places: 5, 7, 2 and 5. Only 42 ends in 2, an even digit, so 42 is even.

mcqs.q: What are the odd numbers from 70 to 90? Which one is in the list?
mcqs.why: Odd numbers from 70 go 71, 73, 75, 77, 79, 81. 81 ends in 1, so 81 is in the list.

mcqs.q: True or false: 15 is an odd number.
mcqs.why: 15 ends in 5 at the ones place. 5 is an odd digit, so 15 is odd and the statement is true.

mcqs.q: After 50, the first four odd numbers are 51, 53, 55 and __. What is missing?
mcqs.why: Odd numbers keep adding 2: 51, 53, 55, then 55 + 2 = 57, so the missing number is 57.

lessons.title: Place Value of Digits
lessons.notes_html:
Place value of a digit

The place value of a digit tells how much the digit is worth in its place: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands and so on. In 245, 5 is at the ones place, so its place value is 5. In 8062, 8 is at the thousands place, so its place value is 8000.

5806 = 5 thousands + 8 hundreds + 0 tens + 6 ones

Worked example

Find the place value of 3 in 2436.

Step 1: In 2436, 3 is at the tens place.

Step 2: 3 tens = 30.

Answer: The place value of 3 is 30. Note: the solved book prints the place value of 2 in 72081 as 200, but 2 is at the thousands place, so the correct place value is 2000.

Key points

  • Read places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands.
  • Place value = digit x value of its place.
  • In 49674, 4 at ten thousands place = 40000.

mcqs.q: In 245, what is the place value of 5?
mcqs.why: In 245, 5 is at the ones place. So its place value is 5 ones, which is 5.

mcqs.q: In 8062, what is the place value of 8?
mcqs.why: In 8062, 8 is at the thousands place. So its place value is 8 thousands, which is 8000.

mcqs.q: 5806 = __ thousands + 8 hundreds + 0 tens + 6 ones. What is missing?
mcqs.why: In 5806, the first digit 5 is at the thousands place, so 5806 has 5 thousands.

mcqs.q: In 2436, what is the place value of 3?
mcqs.why: In 2436, 3 is at the tens place. So 3 tens = 30, and the place value of 3 is 30.

mcqs.q: In 54123, what is the place value of 4?
mcqs.why: In 54123, 4 is at the thousands place. So 4 thousands = 4000, and the place value is 4000.

mcqs.q: In 612378, what is the place value of 8?
mcqs.why: In 612378, 8 is at the ones place at the end. So 8 ones = 8, and the place value is 8.

mcqs.q: In 72081, what is the correct place value of 2?
mcqs.why: Count places in 72081: 2 is at the thousands place. So 2 thousands = 2000. The book printing of 200 is a misprint.

mcqs.q: In 94123, what is the place value of 9?
mcqs.why: In 94123, 9 is at the ten thousands place. So 9 ten thousands = 90000.

mcqs.q: 51001 = 5 ten thousands + __ thousands + 0 hundreds + 0 tens + 1 ones. What is missing?
mcqs.why: In 51001, the second digit 1 is at the thousands place, so there is 1 thousand.

mcqs.q: In 810703, what is the place value of the boxed 0 at the thousands place?
mcqs.why: The boxed 0 is at the thousands place. 0 thousands = 0, so its place value is 0.

lessons.title: Place Value up to Hundred Thousands
lessons.notes_html:
Six places

Big numbers use six places: H-Th (hundred thousands), T-Th (ten thousands), Th (thousands), H (hundreds), T (tens), O (ones). If a number has fewer digits, the empty left places are 0.

Six thousand four hundred forty two is 6442, so H-Th = 0, T-Th = 0, Th = 6, H = 4, T = 4, O = 2.

Worked example

Complete the table for twenty five thousand six hundred thirty one.

Step 1: Write the number in figures: 25631.

Step 2: Read each place: H-Th = 0, T-Th = 2, Th = 5, H = 6, T = 3, O = 1.

Answer: H-Th = 0, T-Th = 2, Th = 5, H = 6, T = 3, O = 1.

Key points

  • Greatest 4-digit number = 9999; smallest 5-digit number = 10000.
  • Greatest 5-digit number = 99999.
  • Greatest 6-digit number = 999999.

mcqs.q: For 6442, what is the H-Th digit?
mcqs.why: 6442 has only 4 digits, so there is no hundred thousands digit. The H-Th place is empty, so it is 0.

mcqs.q: For 25631, what is the Th digit?
mcqs.why: In 25631, read the places: T-Th = 2, Th = 5, H = 6, T = 3, O = 1. So the Th digit is 5.

mcqs.q: Ninety two thousand two is which number?
mcqs.why: Ninety two thousand is 92000 and two more makes 92002. So the number is 92002.

mcqs.q: For 523500, what is the T-Th digit?
mcqs.why: In 523500, H-Th = 5, T-Th = 2, Th = 3, H = 5, T = 0, O = 0. So the T-Th digit is 2.

mcqs.q: What is the greatest 4-digit number?
mcqs.why: The greatest digit is 9. Write 9 four times to get the greatest 4-digit number, 9999.

mcqs.q: What is the smallest 5-digit number?
mcqs.why: The number just after 9999 is 9999 + 1 = 10000, which is the smallest 5-digit number.

mcqs.q: What is the greatest 5-digit number?
mcqs.why: The greatest digit is 9. Write 9 five times to get the greatest 5-digit number, 99999.

mcqs.q: What is the greatest 6-digit number?
mcqs.why: The greatest digit is 9. Write 9 six times to get the greatest 6-digit number, 999999.

mcqs.q: For 92002, what is the T digit?
mcqs.why: In 92002, T-Th = 9, Th = 2, H = 0, T = 0, O = 2. So the tens digit T is 0.

mcqs.q: For 523500, what is the H digit?
mcqs.why: In 523500, H-Th = 5, T-Th = 2, Th = 3, H = 5, T = 0, O = 0. So the hundreds digit H is 5.

lessons.title: Reading and Writing Big Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Reading numbers in words

To read a number, split it into the thousands part and the rest, then read place by place. For example, 4156 is four thousand one hundred fifty six, and 35678 is thirty five thousand six hundred seventy eight.

5060 = Five thousand sixty

Zeros are not read. In 5060 there are no hundreds and no ones, so we only say five thousand sixty. In 7120 we say seven thousand one hundred twenty.

Worked example

Write in figures: eight thousand four hundred sixty one.

Step 1: Eight thousand = 8000 and four hundred = 400.

Step 2: Sixty one = 61. Add: 8000 + 400 + 61 = 8461.

Answer: 8461. Also, fifty five thousand one = 55001.

Key points

  • 123456 = one hundred twenty three thousand four hundred fifty six.
  • 981254 = nine hundred eighty one thousand two hundred fifty four.
  • Write figures by adding each part.

mcqs.q: How do we write 4156 in words?
options: Four thousand one hundred fifty six
mcqs.why: Read place by place: 4 thousands, 1 hundred, 5 tens and 6 ones gives four thousand one hundred fifty six.

mcqs.q: How do we write 5060 in words?
mcqs.why: 5060 has 5 thousands and 6 tens, with no hundreds and no ones. So it is five thousand sixty.

mcqs.q: How do we write 7120 in words?
mcqs.why: 7120 has 7 thousands, 1 hundred and 2 tens, with no ones. So it is seven thousand one hundred twenty.

mcqs.q: Eight thousand four hundred sixty one in figures is:
mcqs.why: Add the parts: 8000 + 400 + 61 = 8461. So the number in figures is 8461.

mcqs.q: Seventy two thousand six hundred ninety five in figures is:
mcqs.why: Add the parts: 72000 + 600 + 95 = 72695. So the number in figures is 72695.

mcqs.q: Fifty five thousand one in figures is:
mcqs.why: Add the parts: 55000 + 1 = 55001. So fifty five thousand one is 55001 in figures.

mcqs.q: How do we write 35678 in words?
options: Three thousand five hundred seventy eight
Thirty five thousand six hundred seventy eight
mcqs.why: 35 is the thousands part and 678 is the rest. So 35678 is thirty five thousand six hundred seventy eight.

mcqs.q: How do we write 41524 in words?
options: Forty one thousand five hundred twenty
Forty one thousand five hundred twenty four
mcqs.why: 41 is the thousands part and 524 is the rest. So 41524 is forty one thousand five hundred twenty four.

mcqs.q: How do we write 123456 in words?
options: One hundred twenty three thousand four hundred fifty six
Twelve thousand three hundred forty five
One hundred twenty three four hundred fifty six
mcqs.why: 123 is the thousands part and 456 is the rest. So 123456 is one hundred twenty three thousand four hundred fifty six.

mcqs.q: How do we write 356782 in words?
options: Thirty five thousand six hundred seventy eight
Three hundred fifty six thousand seven hundred eighty two
Three thousand five hundred sixty seven
Thirty six thousand seven hundred eighty two
mcqs.why: 356 is the thousands part and 782 is the rest. So 356782 is three hundred fifty six thousand seven hundred eighty two.

lessons.title: Number Names, Blanks and Patterns
lessons.notes_html:
Before, after and between

The number before means one less, the number after means one more, and the number between sits in the middle when we count.

Number before 951 = 950, number after 25645 = 25646, and the number between 5420 and 5422 is 5421.

Worked example

Continue the pattern: 2124, 3124, 4124, __, __, __.

Step 1: Each number is 1000 more than the one before it.

Step 2: 4124 + 1000 = 5124, then 6124, then 7124.

Answer: 5124, 6124, 7124. In another pattern each number grows by 10: 51427, 51437, 51447, 51457, 51467, 51477.

Key points

  • Before = subtract 1; after = add 1.
  • Find the jump first, then continue the pattern.
  • 123456, 223456, 323456 grows by 100000 each time.

mcqs.q: What is the number before 951?
mcqs.why: The number before means one less. So 951 - 1 = 950, and the number before 951 is 950.

mcqs.q: What is the number after 25645?
mcqs.why: The number after means one more. So 25645 + 1 = 25646, and the number after is 25646.

mcqs.q: What is the number between 5420 and 5422?
mcqs.why: Count on from 5420: 5420, 5421, 5422. The middle number is 5421.

mcqs.q: Continue: 2124, 3124, 4124, __. What comes next?
mcqs.why: Each number is 1000 more than the one before. So 4124 + 1000 = 5124 comes next.

mcqs.q: Continue: 51427, 51437, 51447, __. What comes next?
mcqs.why: Each number is 10 more than the one before. So 51447 + 10 = 51457 comes next.

mcqs.q: Continue: 123456, 223456, 323456, __. What comes next?
mcqs.why: Each number is 100000 more than the one before. So 323456 + 100000 = 423456 comes next.

mcqs.q: Continue the +1000 pattern fully: after 5124 and 6124 comes __.
mcqs.why: Keep adding 1000: 5124, 6124, then 6124 + 1000 = 7124, so 7124 comes next.

mcqs.q: Continue the +10 pattern: after 51457 and 51467 comes __.
mcqs.why: Keep adding 10: 51457, 51467, then 51467 + 10 = 51477, so 51477 comes next.

mcqs.q: Continue the +100000 pattern: after 423456 and 523456 comes __.
What is 951 - 1?
mcqs.why: Subtracting 1 gives the number just before 951. 951 - 1 = 950.

lessons.title: Comparing Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Comparing numbers

We compare with symbols: < means less than, > means greater than and = means equal to. First count digits: a number with more digits is bigger. So 504 > 99, and 98 < 123 because 98 has 2 digits and 123 has 3 digits.

If digits are equal, compare from the left until digits differ. In 67835 and 67541, the first different digits are 8 and 5, and 8 > 5, so 67835 > 67541.

Worked example

Compare 5421 and 5418.

Step 1: Both have 5 thousands and 4 hundreds.

Step 2: Compare tens: 2 is more than 1.

Answer: 5421 > 5418. Also 5 > 3, 36 < 47 and 3105 = 3105.

Key points

  • More digits means a bigger number.
  • Same digits: compare from the left.
  • Equal numbers use the = sign.

mcqs.q: Use a symbol: 5 __ 3
mcqs.why: 5 is more than 3, and the symbol for greater than is >. So 5 > 3.

mcqs.q: Use a symbol: 36 __ 47
mcqs.why: 36 is less than 47, and the symbol for less than is <. So 36 < 47.

mcqs.q: Use a symbol: 245 __ 3167
mcqs.why: 245 has 3 digits and 3167 has 4 digits. Fewer digits means smaller, so 245 < 3167.

mcqs.q: Use a symbol: 3105 __ 3105
mcqs.why: Both numbers are exactly the same, digit by digit. So we use equal to: 3105 = 3105.

mcqs.q: Use a symbol: 5421 __ 5418
mcqs.why: Both have 5 thousands and 4 hundreds. Compare tens: 2 is more than 1, so 5421 > 5418.

mcqs.q: Use a symbol: 672315 __ 871237
mcqs.why: Both are 6-digit numbers. Compare first digits: 6 is less than 8, so 672315 < 871237.

mcqs.q: Use a symbol: 6421 __ 6578
mcqs.why: Both have 6 thousands. Compare hundreds: 4 is less than 5, so 6421 < 6578.

mcqs.q: Use a symbol: 94561 __ 94271
mcqs.why: Both start with 94. Compare hundreds: 5 is more than 2, so 94561 > 94271.

mcqs.q: Compare 98 and 123. Which is correct?
mcqs.why: 98 has 2 digits and 123 has 3 digits. More digits means bigger, so 98 < 123.

mcqs.q: Use a symbol: 960 __ 980
mcqs.why: Both have 9 hundreds. Compare tens: 6 is less than 8, so 960 < 980.

lessons.title: Ascending and Descending Order
lessons.notes_html:
Ascending and descending order

Ascending order means smallest to largest. Descending order means largest to smallest. First use digits: fewer digits means a smaller number. Then compare from the left.

Worked example

Write in ascending order: 476, 52341, 7881, 5034.

Step 1: 476 has 3 digits, so it is smallest.

Step 2: 5034 and 7881 have 4 digits; 5 thousands is less than 7 thousands, so 5034 comes first.

Step 3: 52341 has 5 digits, so it is largest.

Answer: 476, 5034, 7881, 52341.

For descending order, start with the biggest number. For 6432, 3213, 4343 and 7120, compare the thousands digits 7, 6, 4 and 3, so the order is 7120, 6432, 4343, 3213. For 49231, 12349, 94321 and 31249, compare the ten thousands digits, so the order is 94321, 49231, 31249, 12349.

Key points

  • Ascending: 1778, 2346, 2354, 4632.
  • Descending: 7120, 6432, 4343, 3213.
  • Always check digits first, then left digits.

mcqs.q: Write in ascending order: 476, 52341, 7881, 5034. Which comes first?
mcqs.why: 476 has only 3 digits while the others have 4 or 5 digits. Fewest digits means smallest, so 476 comes first.

mcqs.q: Write in ascending order: 476, 52341, 7881, 5034. Which comes last?
mcqs.why: 52341 has 5 digits, more than all the others. Most digits means largest, so 52341 comes last.

mcqs.q: Write in ascending order: 2346, 4632, 2354, 1778. Which comes first?
mcqs.why: All are 4-digit numbers. Compare thousands: 1, 2, 2, 4. 1 is smallest, so 1778 comes first.

mcqs.q: Between 2346 and 2354, which comes first in ascending order?
mcqs.why: Both have 23 at the start. Compare tens: 4 is less than 5, so 2346 comes before 2354.

mcqs.q: Write in descending order: 6432, 3213, 4343, 7120. Which comes first?
mcqs.why: Descending starts with the largest. Compare thousands: 7 is biggest, so 7120 comes first.

mcqs.q: Write in descending order: 49231, 12349, 94321, 31249. Which comes first?
mcqs.why: Compare ten thousands: 9, 4, 3, 1. 9 is biggest, so 94321 comes first in descending order.

mcqs.q: Write in ascending order: 43513, 3451, 53314, 41353. Which comes first?
mcqs.why: 3451 has only 4 digits while the others have 5 digits. Fewest digits means smallest, so 3451 comes first.

mcqs.q: Write in descending order: 120451, 12345, 57401, 10000. Which comes first?
mcqs.why: 120451 has 6 digits, more than all the others. Most digits means largest, so it comes first.

mcqs.q: Write in descending order: 120451, 12345, 57401, 10000. Which comes last?
mcqs.why: Among the 5-digit numbers, 10000 is smaller than 12345 and 57401, so 10000 comes last.

mcqs.q: What does ascending order mean?
mcqs.why: Ascending order means arranging numbers from smallest to largest, like 476, 5034, 7881, 52341.

lessons.title: The Number Line
lessons.notes_html:
The number line

A number line is a straight line with numbers marked at equal distances. Numbers grow as we move to the right. To show a number, count its steps from 0 and mark that point.

On the line 0 to 11, the tick is at 5 and the cross is at 8.

Worked example

Represent 6 on a number line from 0 to 7.

Step 1: Draw a line and mark 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 at equal distances.

Step 2: Count 6 steps from 0.

Step 3: Mark and circle the point at 6.

Answer: 6 is at the sixth mark from 0. The numbers before 5 are 4, 3, 2, 1 and after 5 are 6, 7, 8, 9.

Key points

  • Count from 0 to find any point.
  • On 0 to 13 we can mark 6, 7, 9, 10 and 12.
  • On 11 to 20 we can encircle 14, 16 and 18.

mcqs.q: On the number line 0 to 11, the tick is on which number?
mcqs.why: Count the marks from 0 along the line. The tick is on the mark named 5, so the ticked number is 5.

mcqs.q: On the number line 0 to 11, the cross is on which number?
mcqs.why: Count the marks from 0 up to the cross. The cross is at the 8th mark, so the crossed number is 8.

mcqs.q: To represent 6 on a line 0 to 7, how many steps do we count from 0?
mcqs.why: Each number is one step from 0. To reach 6, count 6 steps from 0 and circle that point.

mcqs.q: Which numbers are marked on the line 0 to 13 in the exercise?
mcqs.why: The exercise asks to mark 6, 7, 9, 10 and 12 at their own points on the line from 0 to 13.

mcqs.q: The middle circle shows 5. What are the four numbers before 5?
mcqs.why: Count backwards from 5: 4, 3, 2, 1. So the circles before 5 are filled with 1, 2, 3, 4 in order.

mcqs.q: The middle circle shows 5. What are the four numbers after 5?
mcqs.why: Count forwards from 5: 6, 7, 8, 9. So the circles after 5 are filled with 6, 7, 8, 9.

mcqs.q: On the line 11 to 20, which numbers are encircled in the exercise?
mcqs.why: Count from 11: circle 14, then count on to circle 16, then count on to circle 18. So 14, 16 and 18 are encircled.

mcqs.q: What comes just after 14 on the number line?
mcqs.why: Count on by one from 14: 14, 15. So the number just after 14 is 15.

mcqs.q: What comes just before 18 on the number line?
mcqs.why: Count back by one from 18: 18, 17. So the number just before 18 is 17.

mcqs.q: On a number line, numbers get bigger as we move in which direction?
mcqs.why: On a number line like 0 to 11, numbers grow as we move to the right, from 0 towards 11.

lessons.title: Addition: Adding Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Adding numbers

Addition means joining numbers to find the total. Always start from the ones, then add the tens, then the hundreds. If a column makes 10 or more, write the ones digit and carry 1 to the next column. In 582 + 137 the tens make 11, so we write 1 and carry 1.

Worked example

Solve 631 + 289.

Step 1: Add the ones: 1 + 9 = 10. Write 0 and carry 1.

Step 2: Add the tens: 3 + 8 = 11, plus the carried 1 makes 12. Write 2 and carry 1.

Step 3: Add the hundreds: 6 + 2 = 8, plus the carried 1 makes 9.

Answer: 631 + 289 = 920.

Key points

  • Always start adding from the ones column.
  • Carry 1 whenever a column total is 10 or more.
  • A sum can grow a new place, like 905 + 182 = 1087.

mcqs.q: What is 43 + 24?
mcqs.why: Add the ones: 3 + 4 = 7. Add the tens: 4 + 2 = 6. Joining the parts gives 67, so the answer is 67.

mcqs.q: What is 431 + 24?
mcqs.why: Add the ones: 1 + 4 = 5. Add the tens: 3 + 2 = 5. Add the hundreds: 4 + 0 = 4, so the answer is 455.

mcqs.q: What is 65 + 24?
mcqs.why: Add the ones: 5 + 4 = 9. Add the tens: 6 + 2 = 8. Joining the parts gives 89, so the answer is 89.

lessons.title: Adding 4-Digit Numbers without Carrying
lessons.notes_html:
Adding 4-digit numbers without carrying

A 4-digit number has thousands, hundreds, tens and ones. In Exercise 9 no column makes 10 or more, so there is no carrying. Add each column on its own, starting from the ones. The same rule works when we add three numbers together, like 3604 + 4242 + 123.

Worked example

Solve 2564 + 1321.

Step 1: Add the ones: 4 + 1 = 5.

Step 2: Add the tens: 6 + 2 = 8.

Step 3: Add the hundreds: 5 + 3 = 8.

Step 4: Add the thousands: 2 + 1 = 3.

Answer: 2564 + 1321 = 3885.

Key points

  • Line up ones under ones and tens under tens.
  • Without carrying, every column stays below 10.
  • For three numbers, add all three digits in each column.
  • Example check: 7245 + 2433 = 9678, column by column.

lessons.title: Adding 4-Digit Numbers with Carrying
lessons.notes_html:
Adding 4-digit numbers with carrying

When a column total is 10 or more, we carry 1 to the next column. Carry from the ones to the tens, from the tens to the hundreds, and from the hundreds to the thousands. Sometimes the thousands also make 10 and we get a 5-digit answer, like 7385 + 2798 = 10183.

Worked example

Solve 4626 + 3394.

Step 1: Add the ones: 6 + 4 = 10. Write 0 and carry 1.

Step 2: Add the tens: 2 + 9 = 11, plus the carried 1 makes 12. Write 2 and carry 1.

Step 3: Add the hundreds: 6 + 3 = 9, plus the carried 1 makes 10. Write 0 and carry 1.

Step 4: Add the thousands: 4 + 3 = 7, plus the carried 1 makes 8.

Answer: 4626 + 3394 = 8020.

Key points

  • Never forget to add the carried 1.
  • Carrying can happen in every column.
  • Three numbers are added the same way, column by column.

lessons.title: Adding in Different Ways and Mental Addition
lessons.notes_html:
Adding in different ways

We can add in more than one way. One way is to split a number to make a round ten: for 15 + 6, split 6 into 5 + 1, make 15 + 5 = 20, then add 1. Another way is to add the tens first and then the ones: for 21 + 11, add 20 + 10 = 30 and 1 + 1 = 2, then join them.

Worked example

Add 16 + 8 mentally.

Step 1: Split 8 into 4 + 4.

Step 2: Add to make a ten: 16 + 4 = 20.

Step 3: Add the rest: 20 + 4 = 24.

Answer: 16 + 8 = 24.

Key points

  • Making a round ten makes adding easy.
  • Add tens and ones separately, then join.
  • Mental sums in Exercise 11 (C) match answers like 44, 68 and 92.
  • Practice set: 10 + 20 = 30, 23 + 12 = 35 and 22 + 22 = 44. Try them!

mcqs.why: Split 8 into 4 + 4. First 16 + 4 = 20 to make a round ten. Then 20 + 4 = 24, so the answer is 24.

mcqs.why: Add the tens: 20 + 10 = 30. Add the ones: 1 + 1 = 2. Join the parts: 30 + 2 = 32, so the answer is 32.

mcqs.why: Add the tens: 2 tens + 2 tens = 4 tens = 40. Add the ones: 5 + 0 = 5. Join: 40 + 5 = 45, so the answer is 45.

lessons.title: Addition Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Addition word problems

In a word problem, words like altogether, in both and total tell us to add. Read the story, pick the numbers, and add them column by column. Rehana's two books have 328 pages and 1034 pages, so we add 328 + 1034 to find the pages in both books.

Worked example

In a village there are 3321 men, 2843 women and 1822 children. What is the total population?

Step 1: Add the ones: 1 + 3 + 2 = 6.

Step 2: Add the tens: 2 + 4 + 2 = 8.

Step 3: Add the hundreds: 3 + 8 + 8 = 19. Write 9 and carry 1.

Step 4: Add the thousands: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6, plus the carried 1 makes 7.

Answer: The total population of the village is 7986.

Key points

  • Altogether and total mean add.
  • Write the unit, like pages, metres or visitors, in the answer.
  • Check the carrying in every column.

mcqs.q: Rehana's books have 328 pages and 1034 pages. How many pages in both?
mcqs.why: Add 328 + 1034. Ones: 8 + 4 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Tens: 2 + 3 + 1 = 6. Hundreds: 3 + 0 = 3. Thousands: 1, so the answer is 1362 pages.

mcqs.why: Add 800 + 1400. Hundreds: 8 + 4 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Thousands: 0 + 1 + 1 = 2. The ones and tens are 0, so the answer is 2200 m.

mcqs.why: Add 236 + 142. Ones: 6 + 2 = 8. Tens: 3 + 4 = 7. Hundreds: 2 + 1 = 3, so the answer is 378 pages.

lessons.title: Subtraction: Subtracting Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Subtracting numbers

Subtraction means taking away to find what is left. Subtract the ones first, then the tens, then the hundreds. If the top digit is smaller, borrow 1 from the next column: 1 ten becomes 10 ones. In 356 - 178 we borrow in both the ones and the tens columns.

Worked example

Solve 625 - 478.

Step 1: Subtract the ones: 5 cannot take away 8, so borrow 1 ten: 15 - 8 = 7.

Step 2: Subtract the tens: 2 tens became 1 ten; 1 cannot take away 7, so borrow 1 hundred: 11 - 7 = 4.

Step 3: Subtract the hundreds: 6 hundreds became 5 hundreds; 5 - 4 = 1.

Answer: 625 - 478 = 147.

Key points

  • Always subtract the smaller number from the bigger number.
  • Borrowing makes the top digit 10 bigger.
  • With a zero, borrow through it, like 702 - 189 = 513.

mcqs.why: Subtract the ones: 8 - 7 = 1. Subtract the tens: 8 - 4 = 4. Joining the parts gives 41, so the answer is 41.

mcqs.why: Subtract the ones: 6 - 4 = 2. Subtract the tens: 7 - 5 = 2. Joining the parts gives 22, so the answer is 22.

mcqs.why: Subtract the ones: 9 - 8 = 1. Subtract the tens: 3 - 3 = 0. Subtract the hundreds: 6 - 0 = 6, so the answer is 601.

mcqs.why: Subtract the ones: 3 - 1 = 2. Subtract the tens: 7 - 5 = 2. Subtract the hundreds: 4 - 1 = 3, so the answer is 322.

mcqs.why: Subtract the ones: 7 - 4 = 3. Subtract the tens: 9 - 7 = 2. Subtract the hundreds: 2 - 0 = 2, so the answer is 223.

mcqs.why: Ones: borrow 1 ten, 16 - 8 = 8. Tens: 5 became 4, borrow 1 hundred, 14 - 7 = 7. Hundreds: 3 became 2, 2 - 1 = 1, so the answer is 178.

lessons.title: Subtracting 4-Digit Numbers without Borrowing
lessons.notes_html:
Subtracting 4-digit numbers without borrowing

In Exercise 14 every top digit is bigger than the digit below it, so we need no borrowing. Subtract the ones, then the tens, then the hundreds, then the thousands, each column on its own. For example, in 4269 - 3032 each column can be subtracted directly.

Worked example

Solve 9968 - 2734.

Step 1: Subtract the ones: 8 - 4 = 4.

Step 2: Subtract the tens: 6 - 3 = 3.

Step 3: Subtract the hundreds: 9 - 7 = 2.

Step 4: Subtract the thousands: 9 - 2 = 7.

Answer: 9968 - 2734 = 7234.

Key points

  • Check each column: the top digit must be bigger.
  • Keep digits in their correct places.
  • Zero can appear in the answer, like 5754 - 2352 = 3402.

lessons.title: Subtracting 4-Digit Numbers with Borrowing
lessons.notes_html:
Subtracting 4-digit numbers with borrowing

When a top digit is smaller, borrow 1 from the column on its left. Borrowing 1 hundred gives 10 tens, and borrowing 1 ten gives 10 ones. With zeros, borrow through them step by step, like 8004 - 4035, where the thousands give a hundred and the hundred gives a ten. In part (C) we also subtract horizontally: subtract 3254 from 7293 means 7293 - 3254.

Worked example

Solve 5423 - 3987.

Step 1: Subtract the ones: 3 cannot take away 7, so borrow 1 ten: 13 - 7 = 6.

Step 2: Subtract the tens: 2 tens became 1 ten; borrow 1 hundred: 11 - 8 = 3.

Step 3: Subtract the hundreds: 4 became 3; borrow 1 thousand: 13 - 9 = 4.

Step 4: Subtract the thousands: 5 became 4; 4 - 3 = 1.

Answer: 5423 - 3987 = 1436.

Key points

  • After borrowing, the lending digit becomes 1 less.
  • Borrow through zeros one step at a time.
  • The answer can have fewer digits, like 3381 - 2645 = 736.

lessons.title: Mental Subtraction and Different Ways
lessons.notes_html:
Mental subtraction strategies

We can subtract in more than one way. Split the number being taken away: for 15 - 6, split 6 into 5 + 1, do 15 - 5 = 10, then 10 - 1 = 9. Or subtract the tens first, then the ones: for 78 - 12, do 78 - 10 = 68, then 68 - 2 = 66. In the Activity chains, we subtract again and again: start at 50, subtract 5, then 10, then 2.

Worked example

Subtract 93 - 27 mentally.

Step 1: Subtract the tens first: 93 - 20 = 73.

Step 2: Subtract the ones: 73 - 7 = 66.

Answer: 93 - 27 = 66.

Key points

  • Splitting to reach a round ten makes subtraction easy.
  • In a chain, use each answer as the next starting number.
  • Small stories use subtraction too: 42 kg rice - 20 kg = 22 kg left.

mcqs.q: What is 15 - 6?
mcqs.why: Split 6 into 5 + 1. First 15 - 5 = 10 to reach a round ten. Then 10 - 1 = 9, so the answer is 9.

mcqs.q: What is 70 - 8?
mcqs.why: Split 70 into 60 + 10. Subtract from the ten: 10 - 8 = 2. Join with the 60: 60 + 2 = 62, so the answer is 62.

mcqs.q: What is 78 - 12?
mcqs.why: Subtract the tens first: 78 - 10 = 68. Then subtract the ones: 68 - 2 = 66, so the answer is 66.

mcqs.q: What is 89 - 26?
mcqs.why: Subtract the tens first: 89 - 20 = 69. Then subtract the ones: 69 - 6 = 63, so the answer is 63.

mcqs.q: What is 56 - 35?
mcqs.why: Subtract the tens first: 56 - 30 = 26. Then subtract the ones: 26 - 5 = 21, so the answer is 21.

mcqs.q: What is 50 - 12?
mcqs.why: Subtract the ones with borrowing: 10 - 2 = 8. The tens 5 became 4, and 4 - 1 = 3, so the answer is 38.

mcqs.q: What is 97 - 18?
mcqs.why: Subtract the ones with borrowing: 17 - 8 = 9. The tens 9 became 8, and 8 - 1 = 7, so the answer is 79.

mcqs.q: What is 100 - 87?
mcqs.why: Borrow through the zeros: ones 10 - 7 = 3, tens 9 - 8 = 1, and the hundreds 1 became 0, so the answer is 13.

mcqs.q: Start at 50. Subtract 5, then 10, then 2. What is the final number?
mcqs.why: Follow the chain step by step: 50 - 5 = 45, then 45 - 10 = 35, then 35 - 2 = 33, so the final number is 33.

mcqs.q: Sania has 42 kg of rice. She gives 20 kg to her sister. How much rice is left?
mcqs.why: Rice left = 42 - 20. Subtract the tens: 4 tens - 2 tens = 2 tens, and the ones stay 2, so 22 kg of rice is left.

lessons.title: Subtraction Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Subtraction word problems

Words like left, still left and yet to be sold tell us to subtract. A shopkeeper has 850 chocolates and sells 480, so we do 850 - 480 to find how many are left. Always subtract the smaller number from the bigger number and write the unit in the answer.

Worked example

A bakery had 4500 packets of cookies. 1862 were sold. How many were left?

Step 1: Subtract the ones: borrow through the zeros: 10 - 2 = 8.

Step 2: Subtract the tens: 9 - 6 = 3.

Step 3: Subtract the hundreds: 4 cannot take away 8, so borrow 1 thousand: 14 - 8 = 6.

Step 4: Subtract the thousands: 4 became 3; 3 - 1 = 2.

Answer: 2638 packets were left.

Key points

  • Left and remaining mean subtract.
  • Check by adding: answer + taken away = starting number.
  • Example check: 370 + 480 = 850 chocolates.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper has 850 chocolates. He sold 480. How many are left?
mcqs.why: Subtract 850 - 480. Ones: 0 - 0 = 0. Tens: borrow 1 hundred, 15 - 8 = 7. Hundreds: 8 became 7, 7 - 4 = 3, so 370 chocolates are left.

mcqs.q: Two notes together are worth Rs 600. One note is Rs 100. What is the other note?
mcqs.why: Other note = 600 - 100. Subtract the hundreds: 6 hundreds - 1 hundred = 5 hundreds, so the other note is Rs 500.

mcqs.q: A factory made 2460 cars. 1946 cars are sold. How many are yet to be sold?
mcqs.why: Ones: borrow, 10 - 6 = 4. Tens: 6 became 5, 5 - 4 = 1. Hundreds: borrow, 14 - 9 = 5. Thousands: 2 became 1, 1 - 1 = 0, so 514 cars are yet to be sold.

mcqs.q: Shamim collected Rs 4950 and spent Rs 2895. How much is still left?
mcqs.why: Ones: borrow, 10 - 5 = 5. Tens: borrow, 14 - 9 = 5. Hundreds: 9 became 8, 8 - 8 = 0. Thousands: 4 - 2 = 2, so Rs 2055 is still left.

mcqs.q: A bakery had 4500 packets of cookies. 1862 were sold. How many were left?
mcqs.why: Ones: borrow through zeros, 10 - 2 = 8. Tens: 9 - 6 = 3. Hundreds: borrow, 14 - 8 = 6. Thousands: 4 became 3, 3 - 1 = 2, so 2638 packets were left.

mcqs.q: A village has 9015 adults and 4386 are men. How many women are there?
mcqs.why: Ones: borrow, 15 - 6 = 9. Tens: borrow through zero, 10 - 8 = 2. Hundreds: 9 - 3 = 6. Thousands: 8 - 4 = 4, so there are 4629 women.

mcqs.q: Which addition checks that 850 - 480 = 370?
mcqs.why: Subtraction is checked by adding the answer to the number taken away: 370 + 480 = 850, which is the starting number of chocolates, so the check is correct.

mcqs.q: Which addition checks that 2460 - 1946 = 514?
mcqs.why: Add the answer to the number taken away: 514 + 1946 = 2460, which is the number of cars made, so the subtraction 2460 - 1946 = 514 is correct.

mcqs.q: How many cars were sold and left together in the factory story: 1946 sold and 514 left?
mcqs.why: Add the two parts back together: 1946 + 514. Ones: 6 + 4 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Tens: 4 + 1 + 1 = 6. Hundreds: 9 + 5 = 14, write 4 carry 1. Thousands: 1 + 1 = 2, so 2460 cars.

mcqs.q: Shamim spent Rs 2895 and Rs 2055 is left. How much did she collect in all?
mcqs.why: Add spent and left: 2895 + 2055. Ones: 5 + 5 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Tens: 9 + 5 + 1 = 15, write 5 carry 1. Hundreds: 8 + 0 + 1 = 9. Thousands: 2 + 2 = 4, so Rs 4950.

lessons.title: Multiplication as Groups and Repeated Addition
lessons.notes_html:
Multiplication as groups

Multiplication is a quick way to count equal groups. In 3 x 4 there are 3 groups with 4 objects in each group. We can count in fours: 4, 8, 12. Multiplication is also repeated addition: 3 x 4 = 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. Counting in 6, 7, 8 and 9 builds the tables of 6, 7, 8 and 9.

Worked example

Find 7 x 5 by counting objects in groups.

Step 1: There are 7 groups and each group has 5 objects.

Step 2: Count in fives: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35.

Answer: 7 x 5 = 35.

Key points

  • The first number tells how many groups there are.
  • The second number tells how many are in each group.
  • Skip counting gives the table: in 6s we get 6, 12, 18, 24.
  • The table of 8 runs 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80.

mcqs.q: There are 3 groups with 4 objects in each group. What is 3 x 4?
mcqs.why: Count in fours for 3 groups: 4, 8, 12. As repeated addition it is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12, so the answer is 12.

mcqs.q: There are 2 groups with 6 objects in each group. What is 2 x 6?
mcqs.why: Count in sixes for 2 groups: 6, 12. As repeated addition it is 6 + 6 = 12, so the answer is 12.

mcqs.q: What is 3 x 3?
mcqs.why: Count in threes for 3 groups: 3, 6, 9. As repeated addition it is 3 + 3 + 3 = 9, so the answer is 9.

mcqs.q: What is 7 x 5?
mcqs.why: Count in fives 7 times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. Seven groups of 5 make 35 in all, so the answer is 35.

mcqs.q: What is 5 x 9?
mcqs.why: Count in nines 5 times: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45. Five groups of 9 make 45 in all, so the answer is 45.

mcqs.q: What is 8 x 3?
mcqs.why: Count in threes 8 times: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24. Eight groups of 3 make 24, so the answer is 24.

mcqs.q: What is 5 x 6?
mcqs.why: Count in sixes 5 times: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30. Five groups of 6 make 30 in all, so the answer is 30.

mcqs.q: Counting in 6: 6, __, __, 24. Which numbers are missing?
mcqs.why: Counting in 6 means adding 6 each time: 6 + 6 = 12, then 12 + 6 = 18, then 18 + 6 = 24, so the missing numbers are 12 and 18.

mcqs.q: What is 6 x 7?
mcqs.why: Count in sevens 6 times: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42. Six groups of 7 make 42 in all, so the answer is 42.

mcqs.q: What is 9 x 7?
mcqs.why: Count in sevens 9 times: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, 63. Nine groups of 7 make 63, so the answer is 63.

lessons.title: Multiplying Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Multiplying a 2-digit number

To multiply a 2-digit number by a 1-digit number, multiply the ones first, then the tens. If the ones make 10 or more, write the ones digit and carry the tens. For 35 x 2, the ones 5 x 2 = 10, so we write 0 and carry 1, then 3 x 2 = 6 plus the carried 1 makes 7.

Worked example

Multiply 53 x 6.

Step 1: Multiply the ones: 3 x 6 = 18. Write 8 and carry 1.

Step 2: Multiply the tens: 5 x 6 = 30, plus the carried 1 makes 31.

Answer: 53 x 6 = 318.

Key points

  • Always multiply the ones before the tens.
  • Add the carried number after multiplying the tens.
  • Without carrying it is simple: 14 x 2 = 28.
  • More practice from Exercise 19: 11 x 6 = 66 and 21 x 7 = 147.

mcqs.q: What is 14 x 2?
mcqs.why: Multiply the ones: 4 x 2 = 8. Multiply the tens: 1 x 2 = 2. Joining the parts gives 28, so the answer is 28.

mcqs.q: What is 31 x 2?
mcqs.why: Multiply the ones: 1 x 2 = 2. Multiply the tens: 3 x 2 = 6. Joining the parts gives 62, so the answer is 62.

mcqs.q: What is 21 x 4?
mcqs.why: Multiply the ones: 1 x 4 = 4. Multiply the tens: 2 x 4 = 8. Joining the parts gives 84, so the answer is 84.

mcqs.q: What is 23 x 3?
mcqs.why: Multiply the ones: 3 x 3 = 9. Multiply the tens: 2 x 3 = 6. Joining the parts gives 69, so the answer is 69.

mcqs.q: What is 35 x 2?
mcqs.why: Multiply the ones: 5 x 2 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Multiply the tens: 3 x 2 = 6, plus the carried 1 makes 7, so the answer is 70.

mcqs.q: What is 53 x 6?
mcqs.why: Multiply the ones: 3 x 6 = 18, write 8 carry 1. Multiply the tens: 5 x 6 = 30, plus the carried 1 makes 31, so the answer is 318.

mcqs.q: What is 83 x 4?
mcqs.why: Multiply the ones: 3 x 4 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Multiply the tens: 8 x 4 = 32, plus the carried 1 makes 33, so the answer is 332.

mcqs.q: What is 64 x 4?
mcqs.why: Multiply the ones: 4 x 4 = 16, write 6 carry 1. Multiply the tens: 6 x 4 = 24, plus the carried 1 makes 25, so the answer is 256.

mcqs.q: What is 37 x 5?
mcqs.why: Multiply the ones: 7 x 5 = 35, write 5 carry 3. Multiply the tens: 3 x 5 = 15, plus the carried 3 makes 18, so the answer is 185.

mcqs.q: What is 14 x 6?
mcqs.why: Multiply the ones: 4 x 6 = 24, write 4 carry 2. Multiply the tens: 1 x 6 = 6, plus the carried 2 makes 8, so the answer is 84.

lessons.title: Multiplication by 0 and Bigger Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Multiplication by 0 and bigger numbers

Any number multiplied by 0 gives 0: 7 x 0 = 0 and 126 x 0 = 0. Also 0 multiplied by any number gives 0, like 0 x 8000 = 0. For bigger numbers we split one number: for 9 x 12, split 12 into 10 and 2, do 9 x 10 = 90 and 9 x 2 = 18, then add. For a number ending in 0, like 35 x 40, first do 35 x 4 = 140, then write one zero: 1400.

Worked example

Multiply 8 x 14.

Step 1: Split 14 into 10 and 4.

Step 2: Multiply the first part: 8 x 10 = 80.

Step 3: Multiply the second part: 8 x 4 = 32.

Step 4: Add the two parts: 80 + 32 = 112.

Answer: 8 x 14 = 112.

Key points

  • Zero times anything is always zero.
  • Splitting makes big multiplications easy.
  • For tens like 40, multiply first, then add the zero.

mcqs.q: What is 7 x 0?
mcqs.why: When any number is multiplied by 0, the answer is always 0. So 7 groups of nothing make 0, and the answer is 0.

mcqs.q: What is 126 x 0?
mcqs.why: When any number is multiplied by 0, the answer is always 0, however big the number is. So 126 x 0 = 0.

mcqs.q: What is 0 x 8000?
mcqs.why: When 0 is multiplied by any number, the answer is always 0. Zero groups of 8000 are still nothing, so the answer is 0.

mcqs.q: What is 2010 x 0?
mcqs.why: When any number is multiplied by 0, the answer is always 0. So even 2010 multiplied by 0 gives the answer 0.

mcqs.q: What is 9 x 12?
mcqs.why: Split 12 into 10 and 2. First 9 x 10 = 90. Then 9 x 2 = 18. Add the two parts: 90 + 18 = 108, so the answer is 108.

mcqs.q: What is 11 x 13?
mcqs.why: Split 13 into 10 and 3. First 11 x 10 = 110. Then 11 x 3 = 33. Add the two parts: 110 + 33 = 143, so the answer is 143.

mcqs.q: What is 14 x 16?
mcqs.why: Split 16 into 10 and 6. First 14 x 10 = 140. Then 14 x 6 = 84. Add the two parts: 140 + 84 = 224, so the answer is 224.

mcqs.q: What is 35 x 40?
mcqs.why: First multiply 35 x 4 = 140. Because 40 is 4 tens, write one zero at the end: 140 x 10 = 1400, so the answer is 1400.

mcqs.q: What is 45 x 27?
mcqs.why: Split 27 into 20 and 7. First 45 x 20 = 900. Then 45 x 7 = 315. Add the two parts: 900 + 315 = 1215, so the answer is 1215.

mcqs.q: What is 92 x 25?
mcqs.why: Split 25 into 20 and 5. First 92 x 20 = 1840. Then 92 x 5 = 460. Add the two parts: 1840 + 460 = 2300, so the answer is 2300.

lessons.title: Multiplication Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Multiplication word problems

When a story has equal groups, we multiply. There are 15 boxes and each box has 6 motor bikes, so the total is 15 x 6. One week has 7 days, so 40 weeks have 40 x 7 days. Look for the words each and in all in the story.

Worked example

A box contains 54 chocolates. How many chocolates are there in 7 such boxes?

Step 1: Total chocolates = 54 x 7.

Step 2: Multiply the ones: 4 x 7 = 28. Write 8 and carry 2.

Step 3: Multiply the tens: 5 x 7 = 35, plus the carried 2 makes 37.

Answer: There are 378 chocolates in 7 boxes.

Key points

  • Each and in all usually mean multiply.
  • Multiply the number in one group by the number of groups.
  • Write the unit, like bikes, days or books, in the answer.

mcqs.q: There are 15 boxes. Each box has 6 motor bikes. How many bikes in all?
mcqs.why: Total = 15 x 6. Multiply the ones: 5 x 6 = 30, write 0 carry 3. Multiply the tens: 1 x 6 = 6, plus 3 makes 9, so there are 90 bikes.

mcqs.q: How many days are there in 40 weeks, if one week has 7 days?
mcqs.why: Days = 40 x 7. First multiply 4 x 7 = 28. Because 40 is 4 tens, write one zero at the end, so there are 280 days.

mcqs.q: There are 8 nests. Each nest has 6 birds. How many birds in all?
mcqs.why: Total = 8 x 6. Count in sixes 8 times: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, so there are 48 birds in all.

mcqs.q: One box has 54 chocolates. How many chocolates in 7 boxes?
mcqs.why: Total = 54 x 7. Ones: 4 x 7 = 28, write 8 carry 2. Tens: 5 x 7 = 35, plus 2 makes 37, so there are 378 chocolates.

mcqs.q: One cone has 3 scoops. How many scoops in 48 cones?
mcqs.why: Total = 48 x 3. Ones: 8 x 3 = 24, write 4 carry 2. Tens: 4 x 3 = 12, plus 2 makes 14, so there are 144 scoops.

mcqs.q: One shelf has 25 books. How many books on 6 shelves?
mcqs.why: Total = 25 x 6. Ones: 5 x 6 = 30, write 0 carry 3. Tens: 2 x 6 = 12, plus 3 makes 15, so there are 150 books.

mcqs.q: Each box has 6 motor bikes. How many bikes in 10 boxes?
mcqs.why: Total = 10 x 6. Ten groups of 6 can be counted in sixes ten times to reach 60, so there are 60 motor bikes.

mcqs.q: One shelf has 25 books. How many books on 2 shelves?
mcqs.why: Total = 25 x 2. Ones: 5 x 2 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Tens: 2 x 2 = 4, plus 1 makes 5, so there are 50 books.

mcqs.q: Each nest has 6 birds. How many birds in 2 nests?
mcqs.why: Total = 2 x 6. Count in sixes 2 times: 6, 12. Two groups of 6 birds make 12 birds in all.

mcqs.q: One cone has 3 scoops. How many scoops in 10 cones?
mcqs.why: Total = 10 x 3. Ten groups of 3 can be counted in threes ten times to reach 30, so there are 30 scoops.

lessons.title: Division and Parts of a Division Sum
lessons.notes_html:
Division and its parts

Division means sharing into equal parts. The number which is divided is the dividend, the number we divide by is the divisor, and the answer is the quotient. In 8 / 2 = 4, the divisor is 2. If something is left over after sharing equally, it is called the remainder; in all the sums of Exercise 23 nothing is left over. Use the tables to divide: 8 x 7 = 56, so 56 / 8 = 7. Bigger sums can be split, like 72 / 6: split 72 into 60 and 12.

Worked example

Divide 85 / 5.

Step 1: Split 85 into 50 and 35.

Step 2: Divide the first part: 50 / 5 = 10.

Step 3: Divide the second part: 35 / 5 = 7.

Step 4: Add the two parts: 10 + 7 = 17.

Answer: 85 / 5 = 17.

Key points

  • Dividend / divisor = quotient.
  • Check division with the matching table fact.
  • Splitting helps with bigger dividends like 99 / 3 = 33.

mcqs.q: What is 56 ÷ 8?
mcqs.why: Think of the table of 8. Since 8 x 7 = 56, sharing 56 into 8 equal parts gives 7 in each part, so the answer is 7.

mcqs.q: What is 32 ÷ 4?
mcqs.why: Think of the table of 4. Since 4 x 8 = 32, sharing 32 into 4 equal parts gives 8 in each part, so the answer is 8.

mcqs.q: What is 54 ÷ 6?
mcqs.why: Think of the table of 6. Since 6 x 9 = 54, sharing 54 into 6 equal parts gives 9 in each part, so the answer is 9.

mcqs.q: What is 45 ÷ 5?
mcqs.why: Think of the table of 5. Since 5 x 9 = 45, sharing 45 into 5 equal parts gives 9 in each part, so the answer is 9.

mcqs.q: What is 72 ÷ 6?
mcqs.why: Split 72 into 60 and 12. Then 60 ÷ 6 = 10 and 12 ÷ 6 = 2. Add the parts: 10 + 2 = 12, so the answer is 12.

mcqs.q: What is 99 ÷ 3?
mcqs.why: Split 99 into 90 and 9. Then 90 ÷ 3 = 30 and 9 ÷ 3 = 3. Add the parts: 30 + 3 = 33, so the answer is 33.

mcqs.q: In 8 ÷ 2 = 4, which number is the divisor?
mcqs.why: The number we divide by is called the divisor. Here we divide 8 by 2, so the divisor is 2.

mcqs.q: In 42 ÷ 7 = 6, which number is the dividend?
mcqs.why: The number which is divided is called the dividend. Here 42 is divided into 7 equal parts, so the dividend is 42.

mcqs.q: In 64 ÷ 8 = 8, which number is the quotient?
mcqs.why: The answer of a division sum is called the quotient. Here the answer of 64 ÷ 8 is 8, so the quotient is 8.

mcqs.q: In 21 ÷ 7 = 3, the number 7 is called the what?
mcqs.why: The number we divide by is called the divisor. Here we divide 21 by 7, so 7 is the divisor in this sum.

lessons.title: Division Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Division word problems

Stories about sharing equally or making equal groups use division. 28 sweets shared equally among 4 children means 28 / 4 for each child. Packing stories also divide: 80 candles packed in packets of 4 means 80 / 4 packets. Use the tables, and split bigger numbers when needed, like 96 / 6: split 96 into 60 and 36.

Worked example

96 bottles are packed in boxes of 6. How many boxes are needed?

Step 1: Number of boxes = 96 / 6.

Step 2: Split 96 into 60 and 36.

Step 3: Divide each part: 60 / 6 = 10 and 36 / 6 = 6.

Step 4: Add the two parts: 10 + 6 = 16.

Answer: 16 boxes are needed.

Key points

  • Shared equally means divide.
  • Packets of the same size also mean divide.
  • Check with multiplication: 16 x 6 = 96 bottles.

mcqs.q: 28 sweets are shared equally among 4 children. How many sweets does each child get?
mcqs.why: Sweets for each child = 28 ÷ 4. Think of the table of 4: 4 x 7 = 28, so each child gets 7 sweets.

mcqs.q: 45 pencils are packed equally in 5 boxes. How many pencils in each box?
mcqs.why: Pencils in each box = 45 ÷ 5. Think of the table of 5: 5 x 9 = 45, so there are 9 pencils in each box.

mcqs.q: 9 children share Rs 63 equally. How much does each child get?
mcqs.why: Money for each child = 63 ÷ 9. Think of the table of 9: 9 x 7 = 63, so each child gets Rs 7.

mcqs.q: A book has 100 pages. Ahmed reads 5 pages daily. In how many days will he finish?
49 notebooks are shared equally among 7 students. How many does each student get?
mcqs.why: Notebooks for each student = 49 ÷ 7. Think of the table of 7: 7 x 7 = 49, so each student gets 7 notebooks.

mcqs.q: 15 litres of milk is filled equally in 5 bottles. How many litres in each bottle?
mcqs.why: Milk in each bottle = 15 ÷ 5. Think of the table of 5: 5 x 3 = 15, so there are 3 litres in each bottle.

mcqs.q: 81 toffees are shared equally among 9 children. How many toffees does each child get?
mcqs.why: Toffees for each child = 81 ÷ 9. Think of the table of 9: 9 x 9 = 81, so each child gets 9 toffees.

mcqs.q: 80 candles are packed in packets of 4. How many packets are made?
mcqs.why: Packets = 80 ÷ 4. Split 80 into 40 and 40: 40 ÷ 4 = 10 and 40 ÷ 4 = 10. Add: 10 + 10 = 20 packets.

mcqs.q: 36 players are divided into teams of 12. How many teams are formed?
mcqs.why: Teams = 36 ÷ 12. Think of the table of 12: 12 x 3 = 36, so 3 teams are formed from the 36 players.

mcqs.q: 6 kg of sugar costs Rs 84. What is the cost of 1 kg of sugar?
mcqs.why: Cost of 1 kg = 84 ÷ 6. Split 84 into 60 and 24: 60 ÷ 6 = 10 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Add: 10 + 4 = 14, so Rs 14.

lessons.title: What is a Fraction?
lessons.notes_html:
Parts of a whole

A fraction shows equal parts of a whole. The number below the line is the denominator. It tells how many equal parts the whole is divided into. The number above the line is the numerator. It tells how many parts are coloured or taken.

In Exercise 26 (A), a figure divided into 10 equal parts with 7 parts coloured shows the fraction 7/10. In Exercise 26 (C), a figure divided into 11 equal parts with 4 parts coloured shows 4/11.

Worked example

A figure is divided into 4 equal parts and 1 part is coloured. Write the fraction of the coloured part.

Step 1: Total parts = 4, so the denominator is 4.

Step 2: Coloured parts = 1, so the numerator is 1.

Answer: The coloured fraction is 1/4, read as one-fourth.

Key points

  • Denominator = total equal parts.
  • Numerator = coloured parts.
  • To colour 3/4, colour 3 out of 4 equal parts.

mcqs.q: A figure is divided into 4 equal parts and 1 part is coloured. What fraction is coloured?
mcqs.why: Total parts are 4 and coloured parts are 1, so the fraction is 1 over 4, written as 1/4.

mcqs.q: A figure is divided into 10 equal parts and 7 parts are coloured. What fraction is coloured?
mcqs.why: Coloured parts 7 go on top and total parts 10 go below, giving the fraction 7/10.

mcqs.q: What is the denominator in the fraction 3/7?
mcqs.why: The denominator is the number below the line. In 3/7 the number below the line is 7.

mcqs.q: What is the numerator in the fraction 5/12?
mcqs.why: The numerator is the number above the line. In 5/12 the number above the line is 5.

mcqs.q: To colour 3/4 of a figure with 4 equal parts, how many parts do you colour?
mcqs.why: The numerator of 3/4 is 3, so you colour 3 out of the 4 equal parts of the figure.

mcqs.q: A figure is divided into 11 equal parts and 4 parts are coloured. What fraction is shown?
mcqs.why: Coloured parts are 4 and total equal parts are 11, so the fraction shown is 4/11.

mcqs.q: How is the fraction 1/6 read in words?
mcqs.why: The numerator 1 is read as one and the denominator 6 as sixth, so 1/6 is one-sixth.

mcqs.q: A figure is divided into 8 equal parts and 7 parts are coloured. What fraction is coloured?
mcqs.why: There are 7 coloured parts out of 8 total equal parts, so the coloured fraction is 7/8.

mcqs.q: To colour 5/8 of a figure with 8 equal parts, how many parts do you colour?
mcqs.why: The denominator 8 shows the total parts and the numerator 5 shows you colour 5 parts.

mcqs.q: In the fraction 2/3, what does the denominator 3 tell us?
options: The whole is divided into 3 equal parts
mcqs.why: The denominator is below the line and tells the total number of equal parts, which is 3 here.

lessons.title: Equivalent Fractions
lessons.notes_html:
Same amount, different fractions

Equivalent fractions look different but show the same amount. In Exercise 27, the figures show that 2/4, 3/6 and 1/2 all colour half of a figure, so 2/4 = 3/6 = 1/2.

Exercise 27 also shows 3/4 = 6/8 = 9/12 = 12/16 and 4/5 = 8/10 = 12/15 = 16/20.

To make an equivalent fraction, multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number. The amount does not change.

Worked example

Write three equivalent fractions of 2/3.

Step 1: Multiply both by 2: 2 x 2 = 4 and 3 x 2 = 6, giving 4/6.

Step 2: Multiply both by 3: 6/9. Multiply both by 4: 8/12.

Answer: Three equivalent fractions of 2/3 are 4/6, 6/9 and 8/12.

Key points

  • Multiply top and bottom by the same number.
  • 1/4 = 2/8 = 3/12 = 4/16.
  • 1/3 is not equivalent to 1/2.

mcqs.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 1/2?
mcqs.why: 2/4 means 2 out of 4 parts, which is half of the figure, the same amount as 1/2.

mcqs.q: Which fraction is equal to 3/6?
mcqs.why: 3 out of 6 parts is half of the whole, and half is also written as the fraction 1/2.

mcqs.q: Multiply the numerator and denominator of 1/4 by 2. What fraction do you get?
mcqs.why: 1 x 2 = 2 and 4 x 2 = 8, so multiplying both parts of 1/4 by 2 gives 2/8.

mcqs.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 2/3?
mcqs.why: Multiply 2/3 by 2 on top and bottom: 2 x 2 = 4 and 3 x 2 = 6, giving 4/6.

mcqs.q: In the set 2/4, 3/6, 1/2 and 1/3, which fraction is NOT equivalent to the others?
mcqs.why: 2/4, 3/6 and 1/2 are all half, but 1/3 is only one third, so it is not equivalent.

mcqs.q: Multiply the numerator and denominator of 3/4 by 3. What fraction do you get?
mcqs.why: 3 x 3 = 9 and 4 x 3 = 12, so multiplying both parts of 3/4 by 3 gives 9/12.

mcqs.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 4/5?
mcqs.why: Multiply 4/5 by 2 on top and bottom: 4 x 2 = 8 and 5 x 2 = 10, giving 8/10.

mcqs.q: Multiply the numerator and denominator of 1/5 by 4. What fraction do you get?
mcqs.why: 1 x 4 = 4 and 5 x 4 = 20, so multiplying both parts of 1/5 by 4 gives 4/20.

mcqs.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 2/6?
mcqs.why: Multiply 2/6 by 3 on top and bottom: 2 x 3 = 6 and 6 x 3 = 18, giving 6/18.

mcqs.q: How do we make an equivalent fraction?
options: Multiply numerator and denominator by the same number
mcqs.why: Multiplying the top and bottom by the same number keeps the amount the same, so the fractions are equivalent.

lessons.title: Proper Fractions and Comparing Fractions
lessons.notes_html:
Proper fractions

A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator, like 2/3, 3/5 and 4/9 in Exercise 28 (A). A fraction whose numerator is equal to or bigger than the denominator, like 7/5, 3/2 or 9/9, is an improper fraction.

Worked example

Compare 1/6 and 3/6 using the signs >, < or =.

Step 1: The denominators are the same (6).

Step 2: Compare the numerators: 1 is less than 3.

Answer: 1/6 < 3/6.

When denominators are the same, the fraction with the bigger numerator is bigger. Equal fractions, like 2/7 and 2/7, take the = sign.

Exercise 28 (B) also gives 7/9 > 6/9, 5/6 > 2/6, 3/9 < 4/9 and 7/11 = 7/11.

Key points

  • Proper: numerator < denominator.
  • Same denominator: compare numerators only.
  • 7/11 = 7/11 and 5/6 > 2/6.

mcqs.q: Which of these fractions is a proper fraction?
mcqs.why: In 4/9 the numerator 4 is smaller than the denominator 9, so 4/9 is a proper fraction.

mcqs.q: Which of these fractions is an improper fraction?
mcqs.why: In 7/5 the numerator 7 is bigger than the denominator 5, so 7/5 is an improper fraction.

mcqs.q: What kind of fraction is 9/9?
mcqs.why: The numerator 9 is equal to the denominator 9, and equal or bigger numerators make an improper fraction.

mcqs.q: Compare 1/6 and 3/6. Which sign goes in the middle?
mcqs.why: The denominators are both 6 and 1 is less than 3, so 1/6 is less than 3/6.

mcqs.q: Compare 3/5 and 2/5. Which sign goes in the middle?
mcqs.why: The denominators are both 5 and 3 is greater than 2, so 3/5 is greater than 2/5.

mcqs.q: Compare 2/7 and 2/7. Which sign goes in the middle?
mcqs.why: Both numerators and both denominators are the same, so the two fractions are exactly equal.

mcqs.q: Compare 8/10 and 5/10. Which sign goes in the middle?
mcqs.why: The denominators are both 10 and 8 is greater than 5, so 8/10 is greater than 5/10.

mcqs.q: Compare 3/9 and 4/9. Which sign goes in the middle?
mcqs.why: The denominators are both 9 and 3 is less than 4, so 3/9 is less than 4/9.

mcqs.q: When two fractions have the same denominator, how do we tell which is bigger?
options: The one with the bigger denominator
The one with the bigger numerator
mcqs.why: With the same denominator, only the numerators are compared, and the bigger numerator gives the bigger fraction.

mcqs.q: Is 12/15 a proper fraction?
mcqs.why: In 12/15 the numerator 12 is smaller than the denominator 15, so it is a proper fraction.

lessons.title: Adding Like Fractions
lessons.notes_html:
Adding fractions with the same denominator

Like fractions have the same denominator. To add them, add only the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Exercise 29 adds fractions this way in parts (A), (B) and (C), including sums shown with figures.

Worked example

Add 1/3 + 1/3.

Step 1: The denominators are the same (3).

Step 2: Add the numerators: 1 + 1 = 2.

Step 3: The denominator stays 3.

Answer: 1/3 + 1/3 = 2/3.

Remember 5/9 + 4/9 = 9/9, and 9/9 means one whole.

Part (B) also gives 4/12 + 5/12 = 9/12 and 6/15 + 7/15 = 13/15, and part (A) gives 9/20 + 10/20 = 19/20.

Key points

  • Add numerators, keep the denominator.
  • Never add the denominators.
  • 3/7 + 5/7 = 8/7 from the figures in part (C).

mcqs.q: What is 1/3 + 1/3?
mcqs.why: The denominators are the same, so add the numerators: 1 + 1 = 2, and the answer is 2/3.

mcqs.q: What is 1/5 + 3/5?
mcqs.why: Add the numerators 1 + 3 = 4 and keep the denominator 5, so the sum is 4/5.

mcqs.q: What is 2/4 + 1/4?
mcqs.why: Add the numerators 2 + 1 = 3 and keep the denominator 4, so the sum is 3/4.

mcqs.q: What is 3/6 + 2/6?
mcqs.why: Add the numerators 3 + 2 = 5 and keep the denominator 6, so the sum is 5/6.

mcqs.q: What is 2/7 + 4/7?
mcqs.why: Add the numerators 2 + 4 = 6 and keep the denominator 7, so the sum is 6/7.

mcqs.q: What is 3/8 + 4/8?
mcqs.why: Add the numerators 3 + 4 = 7 and keep the denominator 8, so the sum is 7/8.

mcqs.q: What is 5/9 + 4/9?
mcqs.why: Add the numerators 5 + 4 = 9, giving 9/9, and 9/9 means one whole.
Add the numerators 3 + 6 = 9 and keep the denominator 11, so the sum is 9/11.

mcqs.q: Using the figures, what is 2/5 + 1/5?
mcqs.why: The figures show fifths. Add the numerators 2 + 1 = 3, so the sum is 3/5.
Add the numerators 8 + 1 = 9 and keep the denominator 10, so the sum is 9/10.

lessons.title: Subtracting Like Fractions
lessons.notes_html:
Subtracting fractions with the same denominator

To subtract like fractions, subtract only the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Exercise 30 uses this rule in parts 1, 2 and 3.

Worked example

Subtract 2/3 - 1/3.

Step 1: The denominators are the same (3).

Step 2: Subtract the numerators: 2 - 1 = 1.

Step 3: The denominator stays 3.

Answer: 2/3 - 1/3 = 1/3.

One sum in part 3 is printed with different denominators: 16/17 - 15/19. The solved book first makes both denominators 323, giving 304/323 - 255/323 = 49/323.

Part 2 also gives 17/19 - 16/19 = 1/19, and part 3 gives 12/13 - 5/13 = 7/13 and 10/11 - 6/11 = 4/11.

Key points

  • Subtract numerators, keep the denominator.
  • Never subtract the denominators.
  • 13/14 - 2/14 = 11/14.

mcqs.q: What is 2/3 - 1/3?
mcqs.why: The denominators are the same, so subtract the numerators: 2 - 1 = 1, giving 1/3.

mcqs.q: What is 4/5 - 2/5?
mcqs.why: Subtract the numerators 4 - 2 = 2 and keep the denominator 5, so the answer is 2/5.

mcqs.q: What is 5/6 - 4/6?
mcqs.why: Subtract the numerators 5 - 4 = 1 and keep the denominator 6, so the answer is 1/6.

mcqs.q: What is 7/8 - 4/8?
mcqs.why: Subtract the numerators 7 - 4 = 3 and keep the denominator 8, so the answer is 3/8.

mcqs.q: What is 6/7 - 4/7?
mcqs.why: Subtract the numerators 6 - 4 = 2 and keep the denominator 7, so the answer is 2/7.
Subtract the numerators 9 - 4 = 5 and keep the denominator 10, so the answer is 5/10.
Subtract the numerators 11 - 7 = 4 and keep the denominator 13, so the answer is 4/13.
Subtract the numerators 13 - 2 = 11 and keep the denominator 14, so the answer is 11/14.
Subtract the numerators 9 - 8 = 1 and keep the denominator 10, so the answer is 1/10.
