lessons.title: Measuring Length: Metre and Centimetre
lessons.notes_html:
Choosing the right unit

We measure length with a ruler or a tape. Small things are measured in centimetres (cm). Big things are measured in metres (m). Very long distances are measured in kilometres (km).

1 m = 100 cm

An ant, a pen and a hairbrush are measured in cm. The height of a tree, a door and a big window are measured in m. The distance from Karachi to Sukkur is measured in km.

Worked example

Length of the toothbrush = ______ cm

Step 1: Place the zero of the ruler at one end of the toothbrush.

Step 2: Read the mark at the other end. It comes to 10.

Answer: The length of the toothbrush is 10 cm.

Key points

  • Start measuring from the zero mark of the ruler.
  • Use cm for small objects like a pen, an eraser and chalk.
  • Use m for a door, a window and a tree, and km for long distances.

mcqs.q: What is the length of the pen measured with a ruler in Exercise 31?
mcqs.why: Place the zero of the ruler at one end of the pen and read the mark at the other end. The mark comes to 6, so the pen is 6 cm long.

mcqs.q: What is the length of the eraser in Exercise 31?
mcqs.why: Place the zero of the ruler at one end of the eraser and read the mark at the other end. The mark comes to 3, so the eraser is 3 cm long.

mcqs.q: What is the length of the carrot in Exercise 31?
mcqs.why: Place the zero of the ruler at one end of the carrot and read the mark at the other end. The mark comes to 7, so the carrot is 7 cm long.

mcqs.q: What is the length of the mobile phone in Exercise 31?
mcqs.why: Place the zero of the ruler at one end of the mobile phone and read the mark at the other end. It comes to 8, so the phone is 8 cm long.

mcqs.q: In which unit is the length of an ant measured?
mcqs.why: An ant is very small, only a few centimetres long. Small lengths are measured in centimetres, so the answer is centimetres (cm).

mcqs.q: In which unit is the height of a tree measured?
mcqs.why: A tree is tall, much taller than a child. Such big heights are measured in metres, so the height of a tree is measured in metres (m).

mcqs.q: In which unit is the distance from Karachi to Sukkur measured?
mcqs.why: Karachi and Sukkur are two far away cities. Long distances between cities are measured in kilometres, so the answer is kilometres (km).

mcqs.q: The length of a science book is measured in ______.
mcqs.why: A science book is a small object, less than one metre long. Small objects are measured in centimetres, so a science book is measured in centimetres.

mcqs.q: The length of a door is measured in ______.
mcqs.why: A door is tall, about two metres. Big lengths like a door are measured in metres, so the length of a door is measured in metres.

mcqs.q: Which statement is correct?
options: A tower is measured in centimetres
A brick is measured in kilometres
A hairbrush is measured in centimetres
A toothpaste tube is measured in metres
mcqs.why: A hairbrush is a small object, so it is measured in centimetres. A tower needs metres, a brick needs centimetres and a toothpaste tube needs centimetres.

lessons.title: Adding Lengths
lessons.notes_html:
Adding lengths

To add lengths, keep the same unit together. Add centimetres with centimetres and metres with metres. In mixed lengths, first add the centimetres, then add the metres.

1 m = 100 cm

Example: 67 cm + 21 cm. Add the ones: 7 + 1 = 8. Add the tens: 6 + 2 = 8. So the sum is 88 cm.

Worked example

11 m 33 cm + 1 m 41 cm = ______

Step 1: Add the centimetres: 33 + 41 = 74 cm.

Step 2: Add the metres: 11 + 1 = 12 m.

Answer: 12 m 74 cm.

Work through every question of the exercise in the same step-by-step way: read the question, choose the operation or the unit, do the working column by column, and write the unit with the answer.

Key points

  • Always write the unit with the answer.
  • Carry to the next column when a column sum is 10 or more.
  • For km and m, add metres first, then kilometres.

mcqs.why: Add the ones first: 7 + 1 = 8. Then add the tens: 6 + 2 = 8. So 67 cm + 21 cm = 88 cm.
Add the ones: 7 + 5 = 12, write 2 and carry 1. Add the tens: 3 + 8 = 11, plus the carried 1 makes 12. So the sum is 122 m.
Add the ones: 8 + 5 = 13, write 3 and carry 1. Add the tens: 2 + 1 = 3, plus the carried 1 makes 4. So the sum is 43 km.
First add the centimetres: 33 + 41 = 74 cm. Then add the metres: 11 + 1 = 12 m. So the answer is 12 m 74 cm.

mcqs.q: 8 m 68 cm + 6 m 31 cm = ?
mcqs.why: First add the centimetres: 68 + 31 = 99 cm. Then add the metres: 8 + 6 = 14 m. So the answer is 14 m 99 cm.
First add the metres: 515 + 436 = 951 m. Then add the kilometres: 35 + 12 = 47 km. So the answer is 47 km 951 m.
Add the ones first: 6 + 3 = 9. Then add the tens: 6 + 2 = 8. So 66 cm + 23 cm = 89 cm.
Add the ones: 8 + 9 = 17, write 7 and carry 1. Add the tens: 1 + 0 = 1, plus the carried 1 makes 2. So the sum is 27 m.
Add the ones: 3 + 8 = 11, write 1 and carry 1. Add the tens: 2 + 1 = 3, plus the carried 1 makes 4. So the sum is 41 km.
First add the centimetres: 5 + 30 = 35 cm. Then add the metres: 44 + 78 = 122 m. So the answer is 122 m 35 cm.

lessons.title: Length Word Problems: Addition
lessons.notes_html:
Word problems on addition

When a problem asks for the total length or the distance in all, we add the lengths. Keep the same unit in the whole sum.

Example: Sana has a ribbon of 65 cm and Ayesha has a ribbon of 38 cm. To find the total, add 65 + 38 = 103 cm.

Worked example

The distance from Karachi to Hyderabad is 170 km and from Hyderabad to Moro is 165 km. What is the distance from Karachi to Moro?

Step 1: Total distance = 170 + 165.

Step 2: Add the ones: 0 + 5 = 5. Add the tens: 7 + 6 = 13, write 3 and carry 1. Add the hundreds: 1 + 1 = 2, plus 1 makes 3.

Answer: 335 km.

Work through every question of the exercise in the same step-by-step way: read the question, choose the operation or the unit, do the working column by column, and write the unit with the answer.

Key points

  • Words like total and in all mean addition.
  • Add column by column and carry when needed.
  • Write the unit, cm, m or km, with the final answer.

mcqs.q: Sana has a ribbon of 65 cm and Ayesha has a ribbon of 38 cm. What is the total length of both ribbons?
mcqs.why: Total length = 65 + 38. Add the ones: 5 + 8 = 13, write 3 and carry 1. Add the tens: 6 + 3 = 9, plus the carried 1 makes 10. So the total is 103 cm.

mcqs.q: The length of a road is 240 m. Another road of 105 m joins it. What is the total length now?
mcqs.why: Total length = 240 + 105. Add the ones: 0 + 5 = 5. Add the tens: 4 + 0 = 4. Add the hundreds: 2 + 1 = 3. So the total length is 345 m.

mcqs.q: The distance from Karachi to Hyderabad is 170 km and from Hyderabad to Moro is 165 km. What is the distance from Karachi to Moro?
mcqs.why: Total distance = 170 + 165. Add the ones: 0 + 5 = 5. Add the tens: 7 + 6 = 13, write 3 and carry 1. Add the hundreds: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. So it is 335 km.

mcqs.q: A boy walks 300 m to the shop, then 785 m to the park and then 500 m to his home. How much distance does he walk in all?
mcqs.why: Total distance = 300 + 785 + 500. First add 300 + 785 = 1085. Then add 1085 + 500 = 1585. So he walks 1585 m in all.

mcqs.q: A boy walks 300 m to the shop and then 785 m to the park. How far has he walked so far?
mcqs.why: Distance so far = 300 + 785. Add the ones: 0 + 5 = 5. Add the tens: 0 + 8 = 8. Add the hundreds: 3 + 7 = 10. So he has walked 1085 m.

mcqs.q: A boy walks 785 m to the park and then 500 m to his home. How far does he walk on these two parts?
mcqs.why: Distance = 785 + 500. Add the ones: 5 + 0 = 5. Add the tens: 8 + 0 = 8. Add the hundreds: 7 + 5 = 12. So he walks 1285 m on these two parts.

mcqs.q: A boy walks 300 m to the shop and then 500 m from the park to his home. What is the sum of these two parts?
mcqs.why: Sum = 300 + 500. Add the hundreds: 3 + 5 = 8, and the ones and tens are both 0. So the sum of these two parts is 800 m.

mcqs.q: Sana's ribbon is 65 cm. How long will it be if a 38 cm ribbon is joined to it end to end?
mcqs.why: Joining end to end means adding: 65 + 38. Add the ones: 5 + 8 = 13, write 3 and carry 1. Add the tens: 6 + 3 + 1 = 10. So the joined ribbon is 103 cm.

mcqs.q: A road of 240 m is joined by another road of 105 m. How many metres of road are there in all?
mcqs.why: In all means add: 240 + 105 = 345. Add the hundreds: 2 + 1 = 3, the tens: 4 + 0 = 4, and the ones: 0 + 5 = 5. So there are 345 m in all.

mcqs.q: What is 170 km + 165 km?
mcqs.why: Add the ones: 0 + 5 = 5. Add the tens: 7 + 6 = 13, write 3 and carry 1. Add the hundreds: 1 + 1 = 2, plus the carried 1 makes 3. So the sum is 335 km.

lessons.title: Subtracting Lengths
lessons.notes_html:
Subtracting lengths

To subtract lengths, keep the same unit together. If a digit is too small, borrow 1 from the next column. In mixed lengths, first subtract the smaller unit, then the bigger unit.

Example: 81 cm - 42 cm. The ones: 1 cannot take away 2, so borrow 1 ten: 11 - 2 = 9. The tens: 7 - 4 = 3. So the answer is 39 cm.

Worked example

58 km 465 m - 29 km 287 m = ______

Step 1: Subtract the metres: 465 - 287 = 178 m.

Step 2: Subtract the kilometres: 58 - 29 = 29 km.

Answer: 29 km 178 m.

Work through every question of the exercise in the same step-by-step way: read the question, choose the operation or the unit, do the working column by column, and write the unit with the answer.

Key points

  • Always subtract the smaller number from the bigger number.
  • Borrow carefully when a digit is too small.
  • Write the unit with the answer, like cm, m or km.

mcqs.why: Subtract the ones: 1 cannot take away 2, so borrow 1 ten: 11 - 2 = 9. Subtract the tens: 7 - 4 = 3. So 81 cm - 42 cm = 39 cm.
Subtract the ones: 8 cannot take away 9, so borrow 1 ten: 18 - 9 = 9. Subtract the tens: 3 - 1 = 2. So 48 km - 19 km = 29 km.
Subtract the ones: 6 cannot take away 8, so borrow 1 ten: 16 - 8 = 8. Subtract the tens: 1 - 0 = 1. So 26 m - 8 m = 18 m.
First subtract the metres: 80 - 48 = 32 m. Then subtract the kilometres: 39 - 17 = 22 km. So the answer is 22 km 32 m.
First subtract the metres: 72 - 50 = 22 m. Then subtract the kilometres: 44 - 26 = 18 km. So the answer is 18 km 22 m.
First subtract the metres: 465 - 287 = 178 m, borrowing in the ones and tens. Then subtract the kilometres: 58 - 29 = 29 km. So the answer is 29 km 178 m.
Subtract the ones first: 6 - 6 = 0. Then subtract the tens: 7 - 3 = 4. So 76 cm - 36 cm = 40 cm.
Subtract the ones: 2 cannot take away 9, so borrow 1 ten: 12 - 9 = 3. The tens become 0. So 12 m - 9 m = 3 m.
Subtract the ones: 5 cannot take away 8, so borrow 1 ten: 15 - 8 = 7. Subtract the tens: 8 - 8 = 0. So 95 km - 88 km = 7 km.
First subtract the metres: 324 - 150 = 174 m. Then subtract the kilometres: 936 - 864 = 72 km. So the answer is 72 km 174 m.

lessons.title: Length Word Problems: Subtraction
lessons.notes_html:
Word problems on subtraction

When a problem asks how much is left or how much taller one thing is, we subtract the smaller length from the bigger length.

1 m = 100 cm

Example: A wire is 50 m long and 35 m is used. Wire left = 50 - 35 = 15 m.

Worked example

The height of father is 2 m 50 cm and the height of his son is 1 m 22 cm. How much taller is the father?

Step 1: Subtract the centimetres: 50 - 22 = 28 cm.

Step 2: Subtract the metres: 2 - 1 = 1 m.

Answer: The father is 1 m 28 cm taller.

Work through every question of the exercise in the same step-by-step way: read the question, choose the operation or the unit, do the working column by column, and write the unit with the answer.

Key points

  • Words like left, used and taller show subtraction.
  • Subtract centimetres first, then metres, in mixed lengths.
  • Check by adding the answer to the smaller length.

mcqs.q: A wire is 50 m long. 35 m of it is used. How much wire is left?
mcqs.why: Wire left = 50 - 35. Subtract the ones: 0 cannot take away 5, so borrow 1 ten: 10 - 5 = 5. Subtract the tens: 4 - 3 = 1. So 15 m of wire is left.

mcqs.q: A lace is 72 cm long. 47 cm is cut off from it. How much lace is left?
mcqs.why: Lace left = 72 - 47. Subtract the ones: 2 cannot take away 7, so borrow 1 ten: 12 - 7 = 5. Subtract the tens: 6 - 4 = 2. So 25 cm of lace is left.

mcqs.q: A ribbon is 1100 m long. 466 m is used. How much ribbon is left?
mcqs.why: Ribbon left = 1100 - 466. Borrowing through the zeros gives ones 10 - 6 = 4, tens 9 - 6 = 3 and hundreds 10 - 4 = 6. So 634 m of ribbon is left.

mcqs.q: Father is 2 m 50 cm tall and his son is 1 m 22 cm tall. How much taller is the father?
mcqs.why: Subtract the centimetres: 50 - 22 = 28 cm. Subtract the metres: 2 - 1 = 1 m. So the father is 1 m 28 cm taller than his son.

mcqs.q: How much is 50 m - 35 m?
mcqs.why: Subtract the ones: borrow 1 ten, so 10 - 5 = 5. Subtract the tens: 4 - 3 = 1. So 50 m - 35 m = 15 m.

mcqs.q: How much is 72 cm - 47 cm?
mcqs.why: Subtract the ones: borrow 1 ten, so 12 - 7 = 5. Subtract the tens: 6 - 4 = 2. So 72 cm - 47 cm = 25 cm.

mcqs.q: Father's height 2 m 50 cm is equal to how many centimetres?
mcqs.why: First change 2 m to centimetres: 2 x 100 = 200 cm. Then add the extra 50 cm: 200 + 50 = 250 cm. So father's height is 250 cm.

mcqs.q: Son's height 1 m 22 cm is equal to how many centimetres?
mcqs.why: First change 1 m to centimetres: 1 x 100 = 100 cm. Then add the extra 22 cm: 100 + 22 = 122 cm. So the son's height is 122 cm.

mcqs.q: Using centimetres, father's height 250 cm minus son's height 122 cm is ______.
mcqs.why: Subtract column by column: 250 - 122. Ones: 0 - 2 needs borrowing, 10 - 2 = 8. Tens: 4 - 2 = 2. Hundreds: 2 - 1 = 1. So the difference is 128 cm, which is 1 m 28 cm.

mcqs.q: A ribbon is 1100 m long. If 400 m is used first, how much ribbon remains before the rest is used?
mcqs.why: Ribbon remaining = 1100 - 400. Subtract the hundreds: 11 hundreds - 4 hundreds = 7 hundreds. So 700 m of ribbon remains at this stage.

lessons.title: Mass: Gram and Kilogram
lessons.notes_html:
Gram and kilogram

The heaviness of a thing is its mass. Light things are weighed in grams (g). Heavy things are weighed in kilograms (kg).

1 kg = 1000 g

Face cream (50 g), a ring (5 g) and a biscuit pack (40 g) are weighed in grams. An iron rod and a rice sack (50 kg) are weighed in kilograms.

Worked example

A bag of carrots weighing 2 ______.

Step 1: A bag of carrots is heavy, more than one kilogram.

Step 2: Heavy things are weighed in kilograms.

Answer: A bag of carrots weighs 2 kg.

Work through every question of the exercise in the same step-by-step way: read the question, choose the operation or the unit, do the working column by column, and write the unit with the answer.

Key points

  • Use g for light things like chillies, tea and a necklace.
  • Use kg for heavy things like flour, potatoes and a baby.
  • Numbers less than 1000 usually go with grams.

mcqs.q: A bag of carrots weighing 2 ______.
mcqs.why: A bag of carrots is heavy, more than one kilogram. Heavy things are weighed in kilograms, so a bag of carrots weighs 2 kg.

mcqs.q: A packet of chillies weighing 100 ______.
mcqs.why: A small packet of chillies is light. Light things are weighed in grams, so a packet of chillies weighs 100 g.

mcqs.q: A bag of flour weighing 10 ______.
mcqs.why: A big bag of flour is heavy. Heavy things are weighed in kilograms, so a bag of flour weighs 10 kg.

mcqs.q: A tin of ghee weighing 500 ______.
mcqs.why: 500 is less than 1000 and a small tin of ghee is light. Light things are weighed in grams, so a tin of ghee weighs 500 g.

mcqs.q: A packet of tea weighing 250 ______.
mcqs.why: A packet of tea is light. Light things are weighed in grams, so a packet of tea weighs 250 g.

mcqs.q: A baby weighing 4 ______.
mcqs.why: A baby weighs a few kilograms. A baby is far heavier than a few grams, so a baby weighs 4 kg.

mcqs.q: A packet of garam masala weighing 50 ______.
mcqs.why: A small packet of garam masala is very light. Very light things are weighed in grams, so the packet weighs 50 g.

mcqs.q: A sack of potatoes weighing 30 ______.
mcqs.why: A sack of potatoes is very heavy. Heavy things are weighed in kilograms, so a sack of potatoes weighs 30 kg.

mcqs.q: A brick is weighed in ______.
mcqs.why: A building brick is heavy. Heavy things are weighed in kilograms, so a brick is weighed in kilograms (kg).

mcqs.q: A necklace is weighed in ______.
mcqs.why: A necklace is very light. Very light things are weighed in grams, so a necklace is weighed in grams (g).

lessons.title: Adding Masses
lessons.notes_html:
Adding masses

To add masses, add numbers in the same unit together: grams with grams and kilograms with kilograms. Add column by column and carry when a column makes 10 or more.

1 kg = 1000 g

Example: 290 g + 305 g. Ones: 0 + 5 = 5. Tens: 9 + 0 = 9. Hundreds: 2 + 3 = 5. So the sum is 595 g.

Worked example

325 g + 477 g = ______

Step 1: Add the ones: 5 + 7 = 12. Write 2 and carry 1.

Step 2: Add the tens: 2 + 7 = 9, plus the carried 1 makes 10. Write 0 and carry 1.

Step 3: Add the hundreds: 3 + 4 = 7, plus the carried 1 makes 8.

Answer: 802 g.

Work through every question of the exercise in the same step-by-step way: read the question, choose the operation or the unit, do the working column by column, and write the unit with the answer.

Key points

  • Keep grams and kilograms separate.
  • Carry carefully from ones to tens to hundreds.
  • Write g or kg with every answer.

mcqs.why: Add the ones: 0 + 5 = 5. Add the tens: 9 + 0 = 9. Add the hundreds: 2 + 3 = 5. So 290 g + 305 g = 595 g.
Add the ones: 4 + 3 = 7. Add the tens: 0 + 1 = 1. Add the hundreds: 5 + 3 = 8. So 504 g + 313 g = 817 g.
Add the ones: 5 + 7 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Add the tens: 2 + 7 + 1 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Add the hundreds: 3 + 4 + 1 = 8. So the sum is 802 g.
Add the ones: 5 + 6 = 11, write 1 and carry 1. Add the tens: 3 + 4 = 7, plus the carried 1 makes 8. So 35 kg + 46 kg = 81 kg.
Add the ones: 4 + 3 = 7. Tens: 1 + 5 = 6. Hundreds: 2 + 4 = 6. Thousands: 1 + 2 = 3. So the sum is 3667 kg.
Add with carrying: ones 6 + 5 = 11, tens 9 + 2 + 1 = 12, hundreds 3 + 7 + 1 = 11, thousands 2 + 5 + 1 = 8. So the sum is 8121 kg.
Add the ones: 0 + 0 = 0. Add the tens: 5 + 0 = 5. Add the hundreds: 3 + 2 = 5. So 350 g + 200 g = 550 g.
Add the ones: 8 + 5 = 13, write 3 carry 1. Tens: 5 + 6 + 1 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Hundreds: 7 + 2 + 1 = 10. So the sum is 1023 kg.
Add the ones: 5 + 0 = 5. Add the tens: 7 + 0 = 7. Add the hundreds: 3 + 9 = 12. So 375 g + 900 g = 1275 g.
Add the ones: 5 + 2 = 7. Tens: 8 + 1 = 9. Hundreds: 4 + 3 = 7. Thousands: 0 + 7 = 7. So the sum is 7797 g.

lessons.title: Mass Word Problems: Addition
lessons.notes_html:
Word problems on adding mass

When a problem asks how much was bought or picked in all, we add the masses. Keep grams with grams and kilograms with kilograms.

Example: Ahmed bought 250 g of red chillies and 350 g of turmeric. Total spices = 250 + 350 = 600 g.

Worked example

Maria bought 2 kg of potatoes, 7 kg of onions and 6 kg of tomatoes. How many kilograms of vegetables did she buy in all?

Step 1: Total vegetables = 2 + 7 + 6.

Step 2: First add 2 + 7 = 9.

Step 3: Then add 9 + 6 = 15.

Answer: She bought 15 kg of vegetables in all.

Work through every question of the exercise in the same step-by-step way: read the question, choose the operation or the unit, do the working column by column, and write the unit with the answer.

Key points

  • The words in all and total mean addition.
  • For three numbers, add two first, then add the third.
  • Write g or kg with the final answer.

mcqs.q: Ahmed bought 250 g of red chillies and 350 g of turmeric. How many grams of spices did he buy in all?
mcqs.why: Total spices = 250 + 350. Add the tens: 5 + 5 = 10, write 0 and carry 1. Add the hundreds: 2 + 3 + 1 = 6. So he bought 600 g of spices in all.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper sold 10 kg of flour in the morning and 10 kg in the evening. How much flour did he sell in all?
mcqs.why: Total flour = 10 + 10. Add the ones: 0 + 0 = 0. Add the tens: 1 + 1 = 2. So he sold 20 kg of flour in all.

mcqs.q: Maria bought 2 kg of potatoes, 7 kg of onions and 6 kg of tomatoes. How many kilograms of vegetables did she buy in all?
mcqs.why: Total vegetables = 2 + 7 + 6. First add 2 + 7 = 9. Then add 9 + 6 = 15. So she bought 15 kg of vegetables in all.

mcqs.q: A farmer picked 28 kg of cotton on Monday and 31 kg on Tuesday. How much cotton did he pick in all?
mcqs.why: Total cotton = 28 + 31. Add the ones: 8 + 1 = 9. Add the tens: 2 + 3 = 5. So he picked 59 kg of cotton in all.

mcqs.q: How much is 250 g + 350 g?
mcqs.why: Add the ones: 0 + 0 = 0. Add the tens: 5 + 5 = 10, write 0 and carry 1. Add the hundreds: 2 + 3 + 1 = 6. So the sum is 600 g.

mcqs.q: Maria bought 2 kg of potatoes and 7 kg of onions. How much is that together?
mcqs.why: Together means add: 2 + 7 = 9. So potatoes and onions together weigh 9 kg, before the tomatoes are added.

mcqs.q: Maria bought 7 kg of onions and 6 kg of tomatoes. How much is that together?
mcqs.why: Together means add: 7 + 6 = 13. Add the ones: 7 + 6 = 13, write 3 and carry 1 ten. So onions and tomatoes together weigh 13 kg.

mcqs.q: A farmer picked 28 kg of cotton on Monday. How much will he have after picking 31 kg more on Tuesday?
mcqs.why: Cotton in all = 28 + 31. Add the ones: 8 + 1 = 9. Add the tens: 2 + 3 = 5. So after Tuesday he will have 59 kg of cotton.

mcqs.q: What is 10 kg + 10 kg?
mcqs.why: Add the tens: 1 ten + 1 ten = 2 tens, and the ones are 0 + 0 = 0. So 10 kg + 10 kg = 20 kg.

mcqs.q: Maria's potatoes 2 kg and tomatoes 6 kg together weigh ______.
mcqs.why: Together means add: 2 + 6 = 8. So Maria's potatoes and tomatoes together weigh 8 kg.

lessons.title: Subtracting Masses
lessons.notes_html:
Subtracting masses

To subtract masses, subtract in the same unit: grams from grams and kilograms from kilograms. If a digit is too small, borrow from the next column.

Example: 496 g - 382 g. Ones: 6 - 2 = 4. Tens: 9 - 8 = 1. Hundreds: 4 - 3 = 1. So the answer is 114 g.

Worked example

812 g - 653 g = ______

Step 1: Subtract the ones: 2 cannot take away 3, so borrow 1 ten: 12 - 3 = 9.

Step 2: Subtract the tens: 0 cannot take away 5, so borrow 1 hundred: 10 - 5 = 5.

Step 3: Subtract the hundreds: 7 - 6 = 1.

Answer: 159 g.

Work through every question of the exercise in the same step-by-step way: read the question, choose the operation or the unit, do the working column by column, and write the unit with the answer.

Key points

  • Subtract the smaller mass from the bigger mass.
  • Borrow step by step when a digit is too small.
  • Write g or kg with every answer.

mcqs.why: Subtract the ones: 2 - 1 = 1. Subtract the tens: 3 - 3 = 0. So 32 kg - 31 kg = 1 kg.
Subtract the ones: 6 - 2 = 4. Subtract the tens: 9 - 8 = 1. Subtract the hundreds: 4 - 3 = 1. So the answer is 114 g.
Ones: borrow, 12 - 3 = 9. Tens: borrow, 10 - 5 = 5. Hundreds: 7 - 6 = 1. So 812 g - 653 g = 159 g.
Ones: borrow, 14 - 5 = 9. Tens: borrow, 11 - 4 = 7. Hundreds: 6 - 3 = 3. So 724 kg - 345 kg = 379 kg.
Subtract the ones: 3 - 2 = 1. Subtract the tens: 2 - 1 = 1. Subtract the hundreds: 8 - 7 = 1. So the answer is 111 kg.
Ones: borrow, 16 - 7 = 9. Tens: borrow, 17 - 9 = 8. Hundreds: 8 - 3 = 5. So 986 g - 397 g = 589 g.
Borrow through the zero: ones 10 - 8 = 2, tens 9 - 4 = 5, hundreds 5 - 3 = 2. So 600 g - 348 g = 252 g.
Subtract the ones: 8 - 5 = 3. Tens: borrow, 12 - 7 = 5. Hundreds: 3 - 1 = 2. So 428 kg - 175 kg = 253 kg.
Subtract the ones: 5 - 5 = 0. Subtract the tens: 4 - 2 = 2. Subtract the hundreds: 3 - 1 = 2. So the answer is 220 g.
Ones: 0 - 0 = 0. Tens: borrow, 10 - 2 = 8. Hundreds: 1 - 1 = 0. So 200 kg - 120 kg = 80 kg.

lessons.title: Mass Word Problems: Subtraction
lessons.notes_html:
Word problems on subtracting mass

When a problem asks how much is left, how much more can be put, or how much heavier one person is, we subtract.

Example: A sack has 68 kg of rice and 53 kg is taken out. Rice left = 68 - 53 = 15 kg.

Worked example

A truck can carry 5000 kg of load. 3550 kg of load is already put in it. How much more load can be put in the truck?

Step 1: More load = 5000 - 3550.

Step 2: Subtract with borrowing: ones 0, tens 5, hundreds 4, thousands 1.

Answer: 1450 kg more load can be put in the truck.

Work through every question of the exercise in the same step-by-step way: read the question, choose the operation or the unit, do the working column by column, and write the unit with the answer.

Key points

  • Words like left, more and heavier show subtraction.
  • Subtract the smaller mass from the bigger mass.
  • Write kg with the final answer.

mcqs.q: A sack has 68 kg of rice. 53 kg is taken out. How much rice is left in the sack?
mcqs.why: Rice left = 68 - 53. Subtract the ones: 8 - 3 = 5. Subtract the tens: 6 - 5 = 1. So 15 kg of rice is left in the sack.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper had 250 kg of sugar. He sold 150 kg. How much sugar is left?
mcqs.why: Sugar left = 250 - 150. Subtract the hundreds: 2 - 1 = 1, the tens: 5 - 5 = 0, the ones: 0 - 0 = 0. So 100 kg of sugar is left.

mcqs.q: A truck can carry 5000 kg. 3550 kg is already put in it. How much more load can be put in the truck?
mcqs.why: More load = 5000 - 3550. Subtracting with borrowing gives ones 0, tens 5, hundreds 4 and thousands 1. So 1450 kg more load can be put in the truck.

mcqs.q: Ikram weighs 30 kg and his little brother weighs 8 kg. How much heavier is Ikram than his brother?
mcqs.why: Difference = 30 - 8. Subtract the ones: 0 cannot take away 8, so borrow 1 ten: 10 - 8 = 2. Subtract the tens: 2 - 0 = 2. So Ikram is 22 kg heavier.

mcqs.q: How much is 68 kg - 53 kg?
mcqs.why: Subtract the ones: 8 - 3 = 5. Subtract the tens: 6 - 5 = 1. So 68 kg - 53 kg = 15 kg.

mcqs.q: How much is 250 kg - 150 kg?
mcqs.why: Subtract the hundreds: 2 - 1 = 1. Subtract the tens: 5 - 5 = 0. Subtract the ones: 0 - 0 = 0. So the answer is 100 kg.

mcqs.q: A truck can carry 5000 kg. If 3000 kg is put in it, how much more load can still be put?
mcqs.why: More load = 5000 - 3000. Subtract the thousands: 5 - 3 = 2, and all other digits are 0. So 2000 kg more load can still be put in the truck.

mcqs.q: Ikram weighs 30 kg. His brother weighs 8 kg. What is 30 kg - 8 kg?
mcqs.why: Subtract the ones: borrow 1 ten, so 10 - 8 = 2. Subtract the tens: 2 - 0 = 2. So 30 kg - 8 kg = 22 kg.

mcqs.q: A sack has 68 kg of rice. If 50 kg is taken out first, how much rice remains at that stage?
mcqs.why: Rice remaining = 68 - 50. Subtract the tens: 6 - 5 = 1, and the ones stay 8 - 0 = 8. So 18 kg of rice remains at that stage.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper had 250 kg of sugar and sold 150 kg. The sugar left is ______.
mcqs.why: Sugar left = 250 - 150 = 100. Subtract column by column: hundreds 2 - 1 = 1, tens 5 - 5 = 0, ones 0 - 0 = 0. So 100 kg is left.

lessons.title: Capacity: Litre and Millilitre
lessons.notes_html:
Litre and millilitre

The amount of liquid a container can hold is its capacity. Small quantities are measured in millilitres (ml). Large quantities are measured in litres (l).

1 l = 1000 ml

A teacup, a shampoo bottle and a spoonful of syrup are measured in ml. A jug, a bucket and an oil drum are measured in l.

Worked example

A juice carton: 90 ml, 900 ml or 2900 ml?

Step 1: A juice carton holds nearly one litre of juice.

Step 2: 90 ml is too little and 2900 ml is too much for a carton.

Answer: The correct capacity is 900 ml.

Work through every question of the exercise in the same step-by-step way: read the question, choose the operation or the unit, do the working column by column, and write the unit with the answer.

Key points

  • Use ml for small quantities like syrup in a spoon (5 ml).
  • Use l for large quantities like water in a tank (100 l).
  • Read the scale mark where the liquid level stops.

mcqs.q: What is the correct capacity of a juice carton?
mcqs.why: A juice carton holds nearly one litre of juice. 90 ml is too little and 2900 ml is too much, so the correct capacity is 900 ml.

mcqs.q: What is the correct capacity of a bleach bottle?
mcqs.why: A bleach bottle is a big bottle holding a large quantity. It holds about 3 litres, so the correct capacity is 3 l.

mcqs.q: What is the correct capacity of a shampoo bottle?
mcqs.why: A shampoo bottle holds a medium quantity of shampoo. 50 ml is too little and 5 l is too much, so the correct capacity is 500 ml.

mcqs.q: Milk in a jug: 9 ______.
mcqs.why: A jug holds a large quantity of milk. Large quantities are measured in litres, so milk in a jug is 9 l.

mcqs.q: Syrup in a spoon: 5 ______.
mcqs.why: A spoon holds only a tiny quantity of syrup. Tiny quantities are measured in millilitres, so syrup in a spoon is 5 ml.

mcqs.q: Water in a water tank: 100 ______.
mcqs.why: A water tank holds a very large quantity of water. Very large quantities are measured in litres, so water in a tank is 100 l.

mcqs.q: Juice in a juice pack: 250 ______.
mcqs.why: A small juice pack holds a small quantity of juice. Small quantities are measured in millilitres, so juice in a pack is 250 ml.

mcqs.q: Medicine in a medicine bottle: 200 ______.
mcqs.why: A medicine bottle holds a small quantity of medicine. Small quantities are measured in millilitres, so the medicine is 200 ml.

mcqs.q: The capacity of a teacup is measured in ______.
mcqs.why: A teacup holds only a small quantity of tea. Small quantities of liquid are measured in millilitres, so a teacup is measured in ml.

mcqs.q: The capacity of an oil drum is measured in ______.
mcqs.why: An oil drum holds a very large quantity of oil. Large quantities of liquid are measured in litres, so an oil drum is measured in l.

lessons.title: Adding Capacities
lessons.notes_html:
Adding capacities

To add capacities, add in the same unit together. In mixed quantities, first add the millilitres, then add the litres.

1 l = 1000 ml

Example: 635 ml + 223 ml. Ones: 5 + 3 = 8. Tens: 3 + 2 = 5. Hundreds: 6 + 2 = 8. So the sum is 858 ml.

Worked example

3 l 218 ml + 2 l 551 ml = ______

Step 1: Add the millilitres: 218 + 551 = 769 ml.

Step 2: Add the litres: 3 + 2 = 5 l.

Answer: 5 l 769 ml.

Work through every question of the exercise in the same step-by-step way: read the question, choose the operation or the unit, do the working column by column, and write the unit with the answer.

Key points

  • Carry when a column sum is 10 or more.
  • If litres are in only one quantity, they stay the same.
  • Write ml or l with every answer.

mcqs.why: Add the ones: 5 + 3 = 8. Add the tens: 3 + 2 = 5. Add the hundreds: 6 + 2 = 8. So 635 ml + 223 ml = 858 ml.
Ones: 2 + 8 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Tens: 6 + 5 + 1 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Hundreds: 5 + 4 + 1 = 10. So the sum is 1020 ml.
Add the ones: 8 + 1 = 9. Add the tens: 9 + 0 = 9. Add the hundreds: 8 + 1 = 9. So 898 l + 101 l = 999 l.
Ones: 9 + 1 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Tens: 2 + 7 + 1 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Hundreds: 7 + 2 + 1 = 10. So the sum is 1000 l.
Ones: 9 + 6 = 15, write 5 carry 1. Tens: 9 + 6 + 1 = 16, write 6 carry 1. Hundreds: 9 + 6 + 1 = 16. So the sum is 1665 ml.
First add the millilitres: 218 + 551 = 769 ml. Then add the litres: 3 + 2 = 5 l. So the answer is 5 l 769 ml.
Add the ones: 0 + 5 = 5. Add the tens: 2 + 7 = 9. Add the hundreds: 3 + 1 = 4. So 320 ml + 175 ml = 495 ml.
Ones: 8 + 7 = 15, write 5 carry 1. Tens: 0 + 4 + 1 = 5. Hundreds: 6 + 7 = 13. So 608 l + 747 l = 1355 l.
First add the millilitres: 340 + 650 = 990 ml. The litres are only in the second quantity, so they stay 5. So the answer is 5 l 990 ml.
First add the litres: 36 + 23 = 59 l. The millilitres are only in the second quantity, so they stay 825 ml. So the answer is 59 l 825 ml.

lessons.title: Capacity Word Problems: Addition
lessons.notes_html:
Word problems on adding capacity

When a problem asks how much liquid there is in both or in all, we add the capacities. Keep millilitres with millilitres and litres with litres.

Example: A bottle has 350 ml of oil and another bottle has 200 ml of oil. Total oil = 350 + 200 = 550 ml.

Worked example

Three drums have 1320 l, 1215 l and 830 l of petrol. How much petrol is there in all the drums?

Step 1: Total petrol = 1320 + 1215 + 830.

Step 2: First add 1320 + 1215 = 2535.

Step 3: Then add 2535 + 830 = 3365.

Answer: There is 3365 l of petrol in all the drums.

Work through every question of the exercise in the same step-by-step way: read the question, choose the operation or the unit, do the working column by column, and write the unit with the answer.

Key points

  • Words like both, in all and now show addition here.
  • For three numbers, add two first, then add the third.
  • Write ml or l with the final answer.

mcqs.q: A bottle has 350 ml of oil and another bottle has 200 ml of oil. How much oil is there in both bottles?
mcqs.why: Total oil = 350 + 200. Add the hundreds: 3 + 2 = 5, and the tens and ones are 5 and 0. So there is 550 ml of oil in both bottles.

mcqs.q: A tank has 15 l of water. 18 l more water is poured into it. How much water is in the tank now?
mcqs.why: Total water = 15 + 18. Add the ones: 5 + 8 = 13, write 3 and carry 1. Add the tens: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. So there is 33 l of water in the tank now.

mcqs.q: Three drums have 1320 l, 1215 l and 830 l of petrol. How much petrol is there in all the drums?
mcqs.why: Total petrol = 1320 + 1215 + 830. First add 1320 + 1215 = 2535. Then add 2535 + 830 = 3365. So there is 3365 l of petrol in all.

mcqs.q: A tanker carried 550 l of water on Monday and 375 l on Tuesday. How much water did it carry in the two days?
mcqs.why: Total water = 550 + 375. Ones: 0 + 5 = 5. Tens: 5 + 7 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Hundreds: 5 + 3 + 1 = 9. So it carried 925 l in the two days.

mcqs.q: How much is 350 ml + 200 ml?
mcqs.why: Add the ones: 0 + 0 = 0. Add the tens: 5 + 0 = 5. Add the hundreds: 3 + 2 = 5. So 350 ml + 200 ml = 550 ml.

mcqs.q: Two drums have 1320 l and 1215 l of petrol. How much petrol is in these two drums?
mcqs.why: Petrol in two drums = 1320 + 1215. Add column by column: 1320 + 1215 = 2535. So these two drums hold 2535 l of petrol.

mcqs.q: Two drums have 1215 l and 830 l of petrol. How much petrol is in these two drums?
mcqs.why: Petrol in two drums = 1215 + 830. Add the hundreds and thousands carefully: 1215 + 830 = 2045. So these two drums hold 2045 l of petrol.

mcqs.q: Two drums have 1320 l and 830 l of petrol. How much petrol is in these two drums?
mcqs.why: Petrol in two drums = 1320 + 830. Add column by column: 1320 + 830 = 2150. So these two drums hold 2150 l of petrol.

mcqs.q: What is 15 l + 18 l?
mcqs.why: Add the ones: 5 + 8 = 13, write 3 and carry 1. Add the tens: 1 + 1 = 2, plus the carried 1 makes 3. So 15 l + 18 l = 33 l.

mcqs.q: What is 550 l + 375 l?
mcqs.why: Add the ones: 0 + 5 = 5. Add the tens: 5 + 7 = 12, write 2 and carry 1. Add the hundreds: 5 + 3 + 1 = 9. So the sum is 925 l.

lessons.title: Subtracting Capacities
lessons.notes_html:
Subtracting capacities

To subtract capacities, subtract in the same unit: millilitres from millilitres and litres from litres. If a digit is too small, borrow from the next column.

Example: 375 ml - 250 ml. Ones: 5 - 0 = 5. Tens: 7 - 5 = 2. Hundreds: 3 - 2 = 1. So the answer is 125 ml.

Worked example

723 l - 259 l = ______

Step 1: Subtract the ones: 3 cannot take away 9, so borrow 1 ten: 13 - 9 = 4.

Step 2: Subtract the tens: 1 cannot take away 5, so borrow 1 hundred: 11 - 5 = 6.

Step 3: Subtract the hundreds: 6 - 2 = 4.

Answer: 464 l.

Work through every question of the exercise in the same step-by-step way: read the question, choose the operation or the unit, do the working column by column, and write the unit with the answer.

Key points

  • Subtract the smaller capacity from the bigger capacity.
  • Borrow through zeros carefully, as in 1000 l - 560 l.
  • Write ml or l with every answer.

mcqs.why: Subtract the ones: 5 - 0 = 5. Subtract the tens: 7 - 5 = 2. Subtract the hundreds: 3 - 2 = 1. So the answer is 125 ml.
Ones: borrow, 13 - 9 = 4. Tens: borrow, 11 - 5 = 6. Hundreds: 6 - 2 = 4. So 723 l - 259 l = 464 l.
Ones: 6 - 2 = 4. Tens: borrow, 12 - 5 = 7. Hundreds: 2 - 1 = 1. Thousands: 5 - 3 = 2. So the answer is 2174 l.
Subtract the ones: 3 - 2 = 1. Subtract the tens: 5 - 1 = 4. Subtract the hundreds: 5 - 3 = 2. So the answer is 241 ml.
Ones: borrow, 14 - 6 = 8. Tens: borrow, 13 - 5 = 8. Hundreds: 8 - 8 = 0. So 944 ml - 856 ml = 88 ml.
Borrow through the zero: ones 10 - 5 = 5, tens 9 - 8 = 1, hundreds 6 - 6 = 0. So 700 ml - 685 ml = 15 ml.
Subtract the ones: 8 - 3 = 5. Subtract the tens: 9 - 8 = 1. Subtract the hundreds: 5 - 4 = 1. So the answer is 115 ml.
Borrow through the zeros: ones 0 - 0 = 0, tens 10 - 6 = 4, hundreds 9 - 5 = 4, thousands 0. So 1000 l - 560 l = 440 l.
Ones: 0 - 0 = 0. Tens: borrow, 13 - 5 = 8. Hundreds: 5 - 4 = 1. So 630 ml - 450 ml = 180 ml.
Subtract the ones: 0 - 0 = 0. Subtract the tens: 9 - 8 = 1. Subtract the hundreds: 4 - 3 = 1. So the answer is 110 l.

lessons.title: Capacity Word Problems: Subtraction
lessons.notes_html:
Word problems on subtracting capacity

When a problem asks how much liquid is left after some is poured out, sold or used, we subtract.

Example: A jug has 550 ml of water and 220 ml is poured out. Water left = 550 - 220 = 330 ml.

Worked example

A drum has 240 l of oil. 198 l is sold. How much oil is left in the drum?

Step 1: Oil left = 240 - 198.

Step 2: Subtract the ones: borrow 1 ten: 10 - 8 = 2.

Step 3: Subtract the tens: borrow 1 hundred: 13 - 9 = 4. Hundreds: 1 - 1 = 0.

Answer: 42 l of oil is left in the drum.

Work through every question of the exercise in the same step-by-step way: read the question, choose the operation or the unit, do the working column by column, and write the unit with the answer.

Key points

  • Words like left, poured out, sold and used show subtraction.
  • Subtract the smaller capacity from the bigger capacity.
  • Write ml or l with the final answer.

mcqs.q: A jug has 550 ml of water. 220 ml is poured out. How much water is left in the jug?
mcqs.why: Water left = 550 - 220. Subtract the ones: 0 - 0 = 0. Tens: 5 - 2 = 3. Hundreds: 5 - 2 = 3. So 330 ml of water is left in the jug.

mcqs.q: A drum has 240 l of oil. 198 l is sold. How much oil is left in the drum?
mcqs.why: Oil left = 240 - 198. Ones: borrow, 10 - 8 = 2. Tens: borrow, 13 - 9 = 4. Hundreds: 1 - 1 = 0. So 42 l of oil is left in the drum.

mcqs.q: A tank has 1200 l of water. 1185 l is used. How much water is left in the tank?
mcqs.why: Water left = 1200 - 1185. Borrowing through the zeros gives ones 10 - 5 = 5 and tens 9 - 8 = 1, with hundreds and thousands 0. So 15 l is left.

mcqs.q: A water tanker has 1400 l of water. It supplies 750 l to a colony. How much water is left in the tanker?
mcqs.why: Water left = 1400 - 750. Tens: borrow, 10 - 5 = 5. Hundreds: borrow, 13 - 7 = 6. Thousands: 0. So 650 l of water is left in the tanker.

mcqs.q: How much is 550 ml - 220 ml?
mcqs.why: Subtract the ones: 0 - 0 = 0. Subtract the tens: 5 - 2 = 3. Subtract the hundreds: 5 - 2 = 3. So 550 ml - 220 ml = 330 ml.

mcqs.q: How much is 240 l - 198 l?
mcqs.why: Subtract with borrowing: ones 10 - 8 = 2, tens 13 - 9 = 4, hundreds 1 - 1 = 0. So 240 l - 198 l = 42 l.

mcqs.q: A tank has 1200 l of water. If 1000 l is used first, how much water remains at that stage?
mcqs.why: Water remaining = 1200 - 1000. Subtract the thousands: 1 - 1 = 0, and the hundreds stay 2. So 200 l of water remains at that stage.

mcqs.q: A water tanker has 1400 l of water. If it supplies 700 l first, how much water remains at that stage?
mcqs.why: Water remaining = 1400 - 700. Subtract the hundreds: 14 hundreds - 7 hundreds = 7 hundreds. So 700 l of water remains at that stage.

mcqs.q: How much is 1200 l - 1185 l?
mcqs.why: Subtract with borrowing through the zeros: ones 10 - 5 = 5, tens 9 - 8 = 1, hundreds 1 - 1 = 0, thousands 1 - 1 = 0. So the answer is 15 l.

mcqs.q: How much is 1400 l - 750 l?
mcqs.why: Subtract with borrowing: ones 0, tens 10 - 5 = 5 after borrowing, hundreds 13 - 7 = 6 after borrowing, thousands 0. So the answer is 650 l.

lessons.title: Reading the Time: a.m. and p.m.
lessons.notes_html:
Reading a clock

A clock has a short hand for hours and a long hand for minutes. Each number on the clock is 5 minutes, so multiply the number by 5. The long hand on 3 means 15 minutes, on 6 means 30 minutes and on 9 means 45 minutes.

a.m. means morning time, from midnight to noon. p.m. means afternoon, evening and night time, from noon to midnight.

Worked example

The short hand is just past 6 and the long hand is on 3. The clock is marked a.m. What is the time?

Step 1: The short hand just past 6 gives the hour 6.

Step 2: The long hand on 3 gives 3 x 5 = 15 minutes.

Answer: The time is 6:15 a.m.

Key points

  • Long hand on 12 means 0 minutes, a full hour.
  • Daily activities also use a.m. and p.m.: wake up 8:50 a.m., playing 3:45 p.m., sleeping 10:30 p.m.
  • Always write a.m. or p.m. with the time.

mcqs.q: The short hand is just past 6 and the long hand is on 3. The clock is marked a.m. What is the time?
mcqs.why: The short hand just past 6 gives hour 6. The long hand on 3 means 3 x 5 = 15 minutes, so the time is 6:15 a.m.

mcqs.q: The short hand is between 5 and 6, close to 6, and the long hand is on 9. The clock is marked p.m. What is the time?
mcqs.why: The short hand between 5 and 6 means the hour is 5. The long hand on 9 means 9 x 5 = 45 minutes, so the time is 5:45 p.m.

mcqs.q: The short hand is exactly on 3 and the long hand is on 12. The clock is marked p.m. What is the time?
mcqs.why: The short hand on 3 gives hour 3. The long hand on 12 means 0 minutes, so the time is exactly 3:00 p.m.

mcqs.q: The short hand is halfway between 4 and 5 and the long hand is on 6. The clock is marked a.m. What is the time?
mcqs.why: The short hand halfway between 4 and 5 means the hour is 4. The long hand on 6 means 6 x 5 = 30 minutes, so the time is 4:30 a.m.

mcqs.q: The short hand is just before 6 and the long hand is on 11. The clock is marked p.m. What is the time?
mcqs.why: The short hand just before 6 means the hour is still 5. The long hand on 11 means 11 x 5 = 55 minutes, so the time is 5:55 p.m.

mcqs.q: The short hand is between 11 and 12 and the long hand is on 8. The clock is marked p.m. What is the time?
mcqs.why: The short hand between 11 and 12 means the hour is 11. The long hand on 8 means 8 x 5 = 40 minutes, so the time is 11:40 p.m.

mcqs.q: The short hand is halfway between 2 and 3 and the long hand is on 6. The clock is marked p.m. What is the time?
mcqs.why: The short hand halfway between 2 and 3 means the hour is 2. The long hand on 6 means 6 x 5 = 30 minutes, so the time is 2:30 p.m.

mcqs.q: The short hand is between 1 and 2, close to 2, and the long hand is on 9. The clock is marked a.m. What is the time?
mcqs.why: The short hand between 1 and 2 means the hour is 1. The long hand on 9 means 9 x 5 = 45 minutes, so the time is 1:45 a.m.

mcqs.q: In the daily activities, playing time has the hour hand between 3 and 4 and the minute hand on 9, marked p.m. What is the playing time?
mcqs.why: The hour hand between 3 and 4 gives hour 3. The minute hand on 9 means 9 x 5 = 45 minutes, so playing time is 3:45 p.m.

mcqs.q: Sleeping time has the hour hand between 10 and 11 and the minute hand on 6, marked p.m. What is the sleeping time?
mcqs.why: The hour hand between 10 and 11 gives hour 10. The minute hand on 6 means 6 x 5 = 30 minutes, so sleeping time is 10:30 p.m.

lessons.title: Time in Words: Quarter Past and Half Past
lessons.notes_html:
Time in words

One hour has 60 minutes. A quarter of an hour is 60 divided by 4 = 15 minutes, and half an hour is 60 divided by 2 = 30 minutes.

When the long hand is on 3 (15 minutes), we say quarter past the hour. When it is on 6 (30 minutes), we say half past the hour. When it is on 9 (45 minutes), only 15 minutes are left, so we say quarter to the next hour.

Worked example

The clock shows 9:45 in the night. Write it in words.

Step 1: 45 minutes means only 60 - 45 = 15 minutes are left to reach 10.

Step 2: 15 minutes before an hour is a quarter to that hour.

Answer: Quarter to 10 o'clock in the night.

Key points

  • 7:15 in the evening is quarter past 7 o'clock in the evening.
  • 6:30 in the morning is half past 6 o'clock in the morning.
  • Quarter past and half past use the hour that has passed; quarter to uses the next hour.

mcqs.q: How many minutes are there in a quarter of an hour?
mcqs.why: One hour has 60 minutes. A quarter of 60 is 60 divided by 4 = 15, so a quarter of an hour is 15 minutes.

mcqs.q: The clock shows 7:15 in the evening. How do we write this time in words?
mcqs.why: 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour and the minutes are past 7, so 7:15 in the evening is quarter past 7 o'clock in the evening.

mcqs.q: The clock shows 6:30 in the morning. How do we write this time in words?
mcqs.why: 30 minutes is half an hour and the minutes are past 6, so 6:30 in the morning is half past 6 o'clock in the morning.

mcqs.q: The clock shows 9:45 in the night. How do we write this time in words?
mcqs.why: At 45 minutes only 15 minutes are left to reach 10. Fifteen minutes before an hour is a quarter, so it is quarter to 10 o'clock in the night.

mcqs.q: How many minutes are there in half an hour?
mcqs.why: One hour has 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 60 divided by 2 = 30, so half an hour is 30 minutes.

mcqs.q: The long hand is on 3 and the short hand is just past 4. How do we say this time in words?
mcqs.why: The long hand on 3 means 3 x 5 = 15 minutes, which is a quarter. The short hand is just past 4, so the time is quarter past 4.

mcqs.q: The long hand is on 6 and the short hand is halfway between 8 and 9. How do we say this time in words?
mcqs.why: The long hand on 6 means 30 minutes, which is half an hour. The short hand is past 8, so the time is half past 8.

mcqs.q: The long hand is on 9 and the short hand is between 2 and 3, close to 3. How do we say this time in words?
mcqs.why: The long hand on 9 means 45 minutes, so only 15 minutes are left to reach 3. Fifteen minutes before 3 is quarter to 3.

mcqs.q: Which clock time is the same as quarter past 7?
mcqs.why: Quarter past means 15 minutes past the hour. Fifteen minutes past 7 is written as 7:15.

mcqs.q: Which clock time is the same as half past 6?
mcqs.why: Half past means 30 minutes past the hour. Thirty minutes past 6 is written as 6:30.

lessons.title: Minutes Past and Minutes To
lessons.notes_html:
Minutes past and minutes to

We can say a time by counting the minutes. For minutes in the first part of the hour we say minutes past the hour that has passed, like 25 minutes past 9 for 9:25.

When the minutes are close to the next hour, we count the minutes left: 60 minus the minutes gives minutes to the next hour. So 12:55 is 5 minutes to 1, because 60 - 55 = 5.

Worked example

Write 12:55 as minutes past or minutes to.

Step 1: The minutes are 55, which is more than half an hour.

Step 2: Minutes left to reach 1 o'clock = 60 - 55 = 5.

Answer: 12:55 is 5 minutes to 1.

Key points

  • 8:30 is 30 minutes past 8 and 1:15 is 15 minutes past 1.
  • 9:25 a.m. is 25 minutes past 9 in the morning.
  • For minutes to, subtract the minutes from 60 and use the next hour.

mcqs.q: How do we write 12:55 in the form minutes past or minutes to?
mcqs.why: The minutes 55 are more than half an hour. Minutes left to reach 1 o'clock are 60 - 55 = 5, so 12:55 is 5 minutes to 1.

mcqs.q: The clock shows 10:35. How do we write this time?
mcqs.why: The hour hand is between 10 and 11, so the hour is 10. The minute hand shows 35 minutes, counted as 35 minutes past 10.

mcqs.q: The clock shows 8:30. How do we write this time?
mcqs.why: The hour hand is halfway between 8 and 9, so the hour is 8. The minute hand shows 30 minutes, so the time is 30 minutes past 8.

mcqs.q: The clock shows 1:15. How do we write this time?
mcqs.why: The hour hand is just past 1, so the hour is 1. The minute hand shows 15 minutes, so the time is 15 minutes past 1.

mcqs.q: How do we write 9:25 a.m. in words?
mcqs.why: The hour is 9 and the minutes are 25, so it is 25 minutes past 9. The a.m. tells us it is in the morning.

mcqs.q: How do we write 11:30 a.m. in words?
mcqs.why: The hour is 11 and the minutes are 30, so it is 30 minutes past 11. The a.m. tells us it is in the morning.

mcqs.q: How do we write 3:40 a.m. in words?
mcqs.why: The hour is 3 and the minutes are 40, so it is 40 minutes past 3. The a.m. tells us it is in the morning.

mcqs.q: How do we write 5:15 a.m. in words?
mcqs.why: The hour is 5 and the minutes are 15, so it is 15 minutes past 5. The a.m. tells us it is in the morning.

mcqs.q: What does '5 minutes to 1' mean on a clock?
mcqs.why: Five minutes to 1 means 5 minutes are left before 1 o'clock. That is 60 - 5 = 55 minutes past 12, written as 12:55.

mcqs.q: What does '30 minutes past 8' mean on a clock?
mcqs.why: Thirty minutes past 8 means the hour 8 has passed by 30 minutes. That time is written as 8:30.

lessons.title: The Calendar
lessons.notes_html:
Using a calendar

A calendar shows the days, dates, weeks and months of a year. Each column has one day of the week at the top, and the dates in a column are 7 apart. To find the day of a date, find the month, find the date, then read the day at the top of its column.

In the model calendar, 23 March is a Sunday, 11 September is a Thursday and 6 September is a Saturday.

Worked example

How many Fridays are there in the month of June?

Step 1: Find June in the model calendar.

Step 2: Read the dates under Friday: 6, 13, 20 and 27.

Answer: There are 4 Fridays in June.

Key points

  • The year begins on Wednesday, 1 January and ends on Wednesday, 31 December.
  • 14 August, Independence Day, falls on a Thursday.
  • The months with 31 days are January, March, May, July, August, October and December.

mcqs.q: Using the model calendar, on which day does 23 March fall?
mcqs.why: Find March in the model calendar and look at the date 23. Its column has Sunday at the top, so 23 March is a Sunday.

mcqs.q: Using the model calendar, on which day does 11 September fall?
mcqs.why: Find September in the model calendar and look at the date 11. Its column has Thursday at the top, so 11 September is a Thursday.

mcqs.q: Using the model calendar, on which day does 31 March fall?
mcqs.why: Find March in the model calendar and look at the date 31. Its column has Monday at the top, so 31 March is a Monday.

mcqs.q: Using the model calendar, on which day does 6 September fall?
mcqs.why: Find September in the model calendar and look at the date 6. Its column has Saturday at the top, so 6 September is a Saturday.

mcqs.q: Using the model calendar, on which day does 27 April fall?
mcqs.why: Find April in the model calendar and look at the date 27. Its column has Sunday at the top, so 27 April is a Sunday.

mcqs.q: Using the model calendar, on which day does 9 November fall?
mcqs.why: Find November in the model calendar and look at the date 9. Its column has Sunday at the top, so 9 November is a Sunday.

mcqs.q: On which day does the calendar year begin, on 1 January?
mcqs.why: Look at 1 January in the model calendar. It falls under Wednesday, so the year begins on Wednesday, 1 January.

mcqs.q: 14 August is celebrated as Independence Day. On which day does it fall this year?
mcqs.why: Find August in the model calendar and look at the date 14. Its column has Thursday at the top, so 14 August falls on a Thursday.

mcqs.q: How many Fridays are there in the month of June?
mcqs.why: In June the dates under Friday are 6, 13, 20 and 27. Counting them gives 4 Fridays in the month of June.

mcqs.q: Which list shows all the months that have 31 days?
options: January, March, April, July, August, October, December
January, March, May, July, August, October, December
January, February, March, May, July, August, December
January, March, May, June, August, October, December
mcqs.why: Check the last date of every month. The months ending at 31 are January, March, May, July, August, October and December.

lessons.title: Adding Hours
lessons.notes_html:
Adding hours

To add hours, add the numbers column by column, just like ordinary addition, and write hours with the answer. Start from the ones, then the tens, then the hundreds. If a column makes 10 or more, write the ones digit and carry 1 to the next column.

Worked example

Add: 29 hours + 38 hours.

Step 1: Add the ones: 9 + 8 = 17. Write 7 and carry 1.

Step 2: Add the tens: 2 + 3 = 5, plus the carried 1 makes 6.

Answer: 29 hours + 38 hours = 67 hours.

Key points

  • 3 hours + 4 hours = 7 hours and 12 hours + 17 hours = 29 hours.
  • 25 hours + 16 hours = 41 hours, because 5 + 6 = 11 needs a carry.
  • 125 hours + 135 hours = 260 hours and 108 hours + 117 hours = 225 hours.
  • Big sums work the same way: 480 hours + 342 hours = 822 hours.

mcqs.q: 3 hours + 4 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Add the numbers: 3 + 4 = 7. The unit stays hours, so 3 hours + 4 hours = 7 hours.

mcqs.q: 12 hours + 17 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Add the ones: 2 + 7 = 9. Add the tens: 1 + 1 = 2. So 12 hours + 17 hours = 29 hours.

mcqs.q: 25 hours + 16 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Add the ones: 5 + 6 = 11, write 1 and carry 1. Add the tens: 2 + 1 = 3, plus the carried 1 makes 4. The answer is 41 hours.

mcqs.q: 32 hours + 18 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Add the ones: 2 + 8 = 10, write 0 and carry 1. Add the tens: 3 + 1 = 4, plus the carried 1 makes 5. The answer is 50 hours.

mcqs.q: 36 hours + 25 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Add the ones: 6 + 5 = 11, write 1 and carry 1. Add the tens: 3 + 2 = 5, plus the carried 1 makes 6. The answer is 61 hours.

mcqs.q: 32 hours + 22 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Add the ones: 2 + 2 = 4. Add the tens: 3 + 2 = 5. So 32 hours + 22 hours = 54 hours.

mcqs.q: 14 hours + 12 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Add the ones: 4 + 2 = 6. Add the tens: 1 + 1 = 2. So 14 hours + 12 hours = 26 hours.

mcqs.q: 108 hours + 117 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Ones: 8 + 7 = 15, write 5 and carry 1. Tens: 0 + 1 = 1, plus 1 makes 2. Hundreds: 1 + 1 = 2. The answer is 225 hours.

mcqs.q: 385 hours + 323 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Ones: 5 + 3 = 8. Tens: 8 + 2 = 10, write 0 and carry 1. Hundreds: 3 + 3 = 6, plus 1 makes 7. The answer is 708 hours.

mcqs.q: 480 hours + 342 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Ones: 0 + 2 = 2. Tens: 8 + 4 = 12, write 2 and carry 1. Hundreds: 4 + 3 = 7, plus 1 makes 8. The answer is 822 hours.

lessons.title: Time Word Problems: Addition
lessons.notes_html:
Word problems with addition

In a word problem, when we need the total time spent on two or more activities, we add the hours. Read the problem, pick out the hours, add them column by column, and write hours with the answer.

Worked example

A worker works 53 hours in one week and 68 hours in the next week. How many hours does he work in the two weeks?

Step 1: Total hours = 53 + 68.

Step 2: Add the ones: 3 + 8 = 11. Write 1 and carry 1.

Step 3: Add the tens: 5 + 6 = 11, plus the carried 1 makes 12.

Answer: He works 121 hours in the two weeks.

Key points

  • Ali studies 13 hours and plays 4 hours: 13 + 4 = 17 hours in all.
  • Fatima reads 3 hours and writes 4 hours: 3 + 4 = 7 hours in all.
  • Three times can be added too: 2 + 4 + 3 = 9 hours.

mcqs.q: Ali studies 13 hours in a week and plays for 4 hours. How many hours does he spend on both activities?
mcqs.why: Total hours = 13 + 4. Add the ones: 3 + 4 = 7, and the tens stay 1, so he spends 17 hours on both activities.

mcqs.q: A worker works 53 hours in one week and 68 hours in the next week. How many hours does he work in the two weeks?
mcqs.why: Total = 53 + 68. Ones: 3 + 8 = 11, write 1 and carry 1. Tens: 5 + 6 = 11, plus 1 makes 12. He works 121 hours.

mcqs.q: Fatima reads a book for 3 hours and writes for 4 hours. How many hours does she spend in all?
mcqs.why: To find the total time we add: 3 + 4 = 7. So Fatima spends 7 hours in all on reading and writing.

mcqs.q: A boy spends 2 hours at school work, 4 hours playing and 3 hours in other work. How many hours does he spend in all?
mcqs.why: Add all three times: first 2 + 4 = 6, then 6 + 3 = 9. So he spends 9 hours in all these activities.

mcqs.q: Ali studies 13 hours and plays 4 hours. Which sum gives the total time?
mcqs.why: We need the total of both activities, and a total is found by adding. So the sum is 13 + 4 = 17 hours.

mcqs.q: Fatima reads for 3 hours in the morning and writes for 4 hours. She then reads again for 2 more hours. How many hours does she spend in all?
mcqs.why: Add all the times together: 3 + 4 = 7, then 7 + 2 = 9. Using the same adding method, she spends 9 hours in all.

mcqs.q: A worker works 68 hours in one week. The next week he works 53 hours. How many hours is that altogether?
mcqs.why: Altogether means add: 68 + 53. Ones: 8 + 3 = 11, write 1 and carry 1. Tens: 6 + 5 = 11, plus 1 makes 12, giving 121 hours.

mcqs.q: A boy plays for 4 hours and does other work for 3 hours. How many hours does he spend on these two activities?
mcqs.why: Total time = 4 + 3 = 7. So the boy spends 7 hours on playing and other work together.

mcqs.q: Which words in a problem tell us to add the hours?
mcqs.why: Words like 'in all' and 'altogether' ask for a total, and a total is found by adding the hours together.

mcqs.q: A student studies 13 hours in one week and 13 hours in the next week. How many hours does he study in the two weeks?
mcqs.why: Total = 13 + 13. Ones: 3 + 3 = 6. Tens: 1 + 1 = 2. So he studies 26 hours in the two weeks.

lessons.title: Subtracting Hours
lessons.notes_html:
Subtracting hours

To subtract hours, subtract column by column and write hours with the answer. If the top ones digit is smaller than the bottom one, borrow 1 ten from the tens column: the ones become 10 more and the tens become 1 less.

Worked example

Subtract: 33 hours - 14 hours.

Step 1: Subtract the ones: 3 cannot take away 4, so borrow 1 ten: 13 - 4 = 9.

Step 2: Subtract the tens: 3 tens became 2 tens; 2 - 1 = 1.

Answer: 33 hours - 14 hours = 19 hours.

Key points

  • 5 hours - 4 hours = 1 hour and 37 hours - 22 hours = 15 hours.
  • 49 hours - 39 hours = 10 hours.
  • 12 hours - 6 hours = 6 hours and 165 hours - 145 hours = 20 hours.
  • Big sums borrow the same way: 723 hours - 486 hours = 237 hours and 995 hours - 578 hours = 417 hours.

mcqs.q: 5 hours - 4 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Subtract the numbers: 5 - 4 = 1. The unit stays hours, so 5 hours - 4 hours = 1 hour.

mcqs.q: 12 hours - 7 hours = ?
mcqs.why: The ones 2 cannot take away 7, so borrow 1 ten: 12 - 7 = 5. So 12 hours - 7 hours = 5 hours.

mcqs.q: 22 hours - 18 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Ones: borrow 1 ten, 12 - 8 = 4. Tens: 2 tens became 1 ten, and 1 - 1 = 0. So the answer is 4 hours.

mcqs.q: 37 hours - 22 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Subtract the ones: 7 - 2 = 5. Subtract the tens: 3 - 2 = 1. So 37 hours - 22 hours = 15 hours.

mcqs.q: 33 hours - 14 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Ones: borrow 1 ten, 13 - 4 = 9. Tens: 3 tens became 2 tens, and 2 - 1 = 1. So the answer is 19 hours.

mcqs.q: 49 hours - 39 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Subtract the ones: 9 - 9 = 0. Subtract the tens: 4 - 3 = 1. So 49 hours - 39 hours = 10 hours.

mcqs.q: 48 hours - 6 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Subtract the ones: 8 - 6 = 2. The tens stay 4 because 6 hours has no tens. So 48 hours - 6 hours = 42 hours.

mcqs.q: 165 hours - 145 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Ones: 5 - 5 = 0. Tens: 6 - 4 = 2. Hundreds: 1 - 1 = 0. So 165 hours - 145 hours = 20 hours.

mcqs.q: 300 hours - 195 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Borrow through the zeros: ones become 10, 10 - 5 = 5. Tens become 9, 9 - 9 = 0. Hundreds become 2, 2 - 1 = 1. Answer: 105 hours.

mcqs.q: 995 hours - 578 hours = ?
mcqs.why: Ones: borrow, 15 - 8 = 7. Tens: 9 became 8, 8 - 7 = 1. Hundreds: 9 - 5 = 4. So 995 hours - 578 hours = 417 hours.

lessons.title: Time Word Problems: Subtraction
lessons.notes_html:
Word problems with subtraction

When a problem asks how many more hours or which journey is faster, we find the difference by subtracting the smaller number of hours from the bigger one. The one who takes less time is faster.

Worked example

Ahmed studies for 22 hours in a week and his brother studies for 15 hours. How many more hours does Ahmed study?

Step 1: Difference = 22 - 15.

Step 2: Subtract the ones: borrow 1 ten, 12 - 5 = 7.

Step 3: Subtract the tens: 2 tens became 1 ten; 1 - 1 = 0.

Answer: Ahmed studies 7 hours more.

Key points

  • A train takes 8 hours and a car 6 hours: the car is faster by 8 - 6 = 2 hours.
  • Azeem reads 9 hours and Aslam 5 hours: Azeem reads 9 - 5 = 4 hours more.
  • Sara starts at 5:00 p.m. and studies 2 hours 30 minutes, so she studies till 7:30 p.m.

mcqs.q: A train takes 8 hours to reach Lahore and a car takes 6 hours for the same journey. Which is faster and by how many hours?
mcqs.why: The car takes less time, so the car is faster. Difference = 8 - 6 = 2, so the car takes 2 hours less than the train.

mcqs.q: Ahmed studies for 22 hours in a week and his brother studies for 15 hours. How many more hours does Ahmed study?
mcqs.why: Difference = 22 - 15. Ones: borrow 1 ten, 12 - 5 = 7. Tens: 1 - 1 = 0. So Ahmed studies 7 hours more.

mcqs.q: Azeem reads for 9 hours and Aslam reads for 5 hours. How many more hours does Azeem read?
mcqs.why: How many more means subtract: 9 - 5 = 4. So Azeem reads 4 hours more than Aslam.

mcqs.q: Student A spends 14 hours on homework and student B spends 20 hours. How many more hours does B spend than A?
mcqs.why: Difference = 20 - 14. Ones: borrow 1 ten, 10 - 4 = 6. Tens: 1 - 1 = 0. So B spends 6 hours more than A.

mcqs.q: It is 5:00 p.m. Sara starts studying and studies for 2 hours and 30 minutes. Till what time does she study?
mcqs.why: Count forward from 5:00 p.m.: after 2 hours it is 7:00 p.m., and after 30 more minutes it is 7:30 p.m.

mcqs.q: For how long does Sara study if she starts at 5:00 p.m. and studies for 2 hours and 30 minutes?
mcqs.why: The time she spends studying is given in the problem itself: she studies for 2 hours and 30 minutes, finishing at 7:30 p.m.

mcqs.q: A train takes 8 hours and a car takes 6 hours. How much time does the train take more than the car?
mcqs.why: Subtract the smaller time from the bigger time: 8 - 6 = 2. So the train takes 2 hours more than the car.

mcqs.q: Ahmed studies 22 hours and his brother studies 15 hours. Which sum finds how many more hours Ahmed studies?
mcqs.why: How many more is a difference, found by subtracting the smaller number from the bigger one: 22 - 15 = 7 hours.

mcqs.q: Student B spends 20 hours on homework and student A spends 14 hours. How many fewer hours does A spend than B?
mcqs.why: Difference = 20 - 14 = 6. So student A spends 6 fewer hours on homework than student B.

mcqs.q: Azeem reads for 9 hours. Aslam reads 4 hours less than Azeem. How many hours does Aslam read?
mcqs.why: Aslam reads 4 hours less, so subtract: 9 - 4 = 5. This matches the exercise, where Aslam reads for 5 hours.

lessons.title: Line, Line Segment and Ray
lessons.notes_html:
Three kinds of straight figures

A line segment is straight and has two end points. It stops at both ends. A ray has one end point and an arrow on the other side, so it goes on in one direction. In the activity, ST, LM, XY and EF are line segments, while BC, AB, MN and PQ are rays. A curved arc and a wavy line are neither.

Worked example

How many end points does the line segment MN have? Name them.

Step 1: A line segment stops at both ends.

Step 2: Segment MN stops at M on one side and at N on the other side.

Answer: Line segment MN has two end points, M and N.

In Exercise 53, the four line segments with the common end point A are AB, AD, AE and AC.

Key points

  • Line segment: 2 end points.
  • Ray: 1 end point and an arrow.
  • A segment can be named PQ or QP.

mcqs.q: Which figure is a line segment?
options: A straight figure with two end points
mcqs.why: A line segment is straight and stops at two end points, which matches the straight figure with two end points.

mcqs.q: How many end points does line segment MN have, and what are they?
options: Two end points, M and N
mcqs.why: A line segment stops at both ends. Segment MN stops at M and at N, so it has two end points.

mcqs.q: How many end points does ray PQ have, and what is it?
options: Two end points, P and Q
mcqs.why: A ray starts at one point and goes on with an arrow. Ray PQ starts at P, so P is its only end point.

mcqs.q: In the activity, ST is which kind of figure?
mcqs.why: ST has two end points and no arrow, so ST is a line segment, not a ray.

mcqs.q: In the activity, BC is which kind of figure?
mcqs.why: BC has an arrow on one side and one end point, so BC is a ray.

mcqs.q: A line segment in a figure can be named in two ways. What are they?
mcqs.why: A segment can be read from either end, so the same segment can be named PQ or QP.

mcqs.q: In one figure, some rays meet at a point marked with a letter. What is that point?
mcqs.why: The rays in that figure start and meet at the point marked with the letter G.

mcqs.q: Four line segments have the same end point A. Which set names them?
mcqs.why: The segments starting from point A go to B, D, E and C, so they are AB, AD, AE and AC.

mcqs.q: What is a curved arc in Exercise 53?
options: Neither a line segment nor a ray
mcqs.why: A line segment and a ray are both straight. A curved arc is not straight, so it is neither.

mcqs.q: With points P, Q and R, which are the line segments formed by joining every pair?
mcqs.why: Joining every pair of points gives P with Q, Q with R and P with R, so the segments are PQ, QR and PR.

lessons.title: 2-D Shapes
lessons.notes_html:
Naming shapes by their sides

A square has 4 equal sides and 4 square corners. A rectangle has 4 sides with opposite sides equal and 4 square corners. A triangle has 3 sides. Any closed shape with 4 sides is a quadrilateral. In Exercise 54 part 1, the shapes are: (a) Square, (b) Quadrilateral, (c) Rectangle, (d) Triangle, (e) Triangle and (f) Square.

Worked example

Complete the sentence: A shape with 4 equal sides is a ______.

Step 1: A shape with 4 equal sides and square corners is a square.

Answer: A shape with 4 equal sides is a Square.

On a dot grid, draw a rectangle by joining 4 dots so opposite sides are equal, and a triangle by joining 3 dots.

Key points

  • Square: 4 equal sides.
  • Rectangle: opposite sides equal.
  • Triangle: 3 sides.

mcqs.q: A shape has 4 equal sides and 4 square corners. What is it?
mcqs.why: All four sides are equal and the corners are square corners, which is exactly a square.

mcqs.q: A shape has 3 sides. What is it?
mcqs.why: Tri means three, and a closed shape with exactly 3 sides is called a triangle.

mcqs.q: A shape has opposite sides equal and 4 square corners, but all sides are not equal. What is it?
mcqs.why: Opposite sides equal with square corners, but not all sides equal, describes a rectangle.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: All the sides of a ______ are equal.
mcqs.why: In a square, all four sides are equal, so the missing word in the sentence is Square.

mcqs.q: What do we call any closed shape with 4 sides?
mcqs.why: Any closed shape with 4 sides is called a quadrilateral, whatever the lengths of its sides are.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: A ______ has 4 sides and its longer sides are opposite each other.
mcqs.why: A rectangle has 4 sides and its opposite sides are equal, with the longer sides opposite each other.

mcqs.q: How many sides does a triangle have?
mcqs.why: A triangle is a 3-sided shape, so the number of sides of a triangle is 3.

mcqs.q: How will you draw a triangle on a dot grid?
options: Join 3 dots with three straight lines
mcqs.why: A triangle has 3 sides, so on the dot grid you join 3 dots with three straight lines.

mcqs.q: How will you draw a rectangle on a dot grid?
options: Join dots to make opposite sides equal
Join dots to make all sides equal
mcqs.why: For a rectangle, join 4 dots to make a shape whose opposite sides are equal, as in the example.

mcqs.q: In Exercise 54, shape (f) has 4 equal sides. What is shape (f)?
mcqs.why: Shape (f) has 4 sides and all of them are equal, so shape (f) is a square.

lessons.title: Parts of a Circle
lessons.notes_html:
Centre, radius and diameter

The point in the middle of a circle is its centre. A line from the centre to the circle is a radius. A line passing through the centre and touching the circle on both sides is the diameter. The radius is half of the diameter.

Diameter = 2 x radius

Worked example

A circle has centre O and the line EF passing through O. Name the centre, diameter and radius.

Step 1: The middle point is O, so the centre is O.

Step 2: EF passes through O and touches the circle on both sides, so EF is the diameter.

Step 3: EO and OF join the centre to the circle, so they are radii.

Answer: Centre = O, Diameter = EF, Radius = EO and OF.

Key points

  • Diameter passes through the centre.
  • Diameter is the longest line in the circle.
  • Radius touches the circle at one point only.

mcqs.q: In a circle with centre O and line EF passing through O, what is EF?
mcqs.why: EF passes through the centre O and touches the circle on both sides, so EF is the diameter.

mcqs.q: In the same circle with centre O, which lines are radii?
mcqs.why: EO and OF each join the centre O to a point on the circle, so both of them are radii.

mcqs.q: A circle has centre M and line SR passing through M. What is the centre?
mcqs.why: The point in the middle of this circle is marked M, so the centre of the circle is M.

mcqs.q: In the circle with centre M, what is SR?
mcqs.why: SR passes through the centre M and touches the circle on both sides, so SR is the diameter.

mcqs.q: A circle has centre C and line AB passing through C. Which lines are radii?
mcqs.why: CA and CB each join the centre C to a point on the circle, so CA and CB are radii.

mcqs.q: What is the centre of a circle?
options: The point in the middle of the circle
mcqs.why: The centre is the point in the middle of the circle, from which radii are drawn to the circle.

mcqs.q: What is a radius of a circle?
options: A line through the centre joining two points on the circle
A line joining the centre to any point on the circle
mcqs.why: A radius joins the centre to any point on the circle and touches the circle at only one point.

mcqs.q: What is a diameter of a circle?
options: A line from the centre to the circle
A line joining two points but not through the centre
A line passing through the centre and joining two points on the circle
mcqs.why: The diameter passes through the centre and joins two points on the circle, touching it on both sides.

mcqs.q: How long is the radius compared with the diameter?
mcqs.why: The line from the centre to the edge is half of the diameter, so the radius is half the diameter.

mcqs.q: Which line is the longest line in a circle?
options: A short line near the edge
mcqs.why: The line passing through the centre is the diameter, and the book calls it the longest line in the circle.

lessons.title: Perimeter of Shapes
lessons.notes_html:
All around a shape

The perimeter of a figure is the total length all around it. To find it, add the lengths of all its sides. A square has 4 equal sides, so its perimeter can be found by multiplying one side by 4.

Worked example

Find the perimeter of a rectangle ZYXW with length 6 cm and width 3 cm.

Step 1: The four sides of the rectangle are 6 cm, 3 cm, 6 cm and 3 cm.

Step 2: Add all four sides: 6 + 3 + 6 + 3.

Step 3: 6 + 3 = 9, 9 + 6 = 15 and 15 + 3 = 18.

Answer: The perimeter of the rectangle is 18 cm.

A triangle DEF with sides 6 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm has perimeter 6 + 4 + 5 = 15 cm.

Key points

  • Perimeter = sum of all side lengths.
  • Square side 3 cm: perimeter 12 cm.
  • Window 75 cm by 50 cm: perimeter 250 cm.

mcqs.q: What is the perimeter of a rectangle with length 6 cm and width 3 cm?
mcqs.why: Add all four sides of the rectangle: 6 + 3 + 6 + 3 = 18, so the perimeter is 18 cm.

mcqs.q: What is the perimeter of a square with each side 3 cm?
mcqs.why: A square has 4 equal sides, so add them: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12 cm perimeter.

mcqs.q: A triangle DEF has sides DE = 6 cm, EF = 4 cm and FD = 5 cm. What is its perimeter?
mcqs.why: Add all three sides of the triangle: 6 + 4 = 10 and 10 + 5 = 15, so the perimeter is 15 cm.

mcqs.q: What is the perimeter of a square table with each side 38 cm?
mcqs.why: The square table has 4 equal sides: 38 x 4 = 152, so its perimeter is 152 cm.

mcqs.q: A window has length 75 cm and width 50 cm. What is its perimeter?
mcqs.why: The window is a rectangle with sides 75, 50, 75 and 50. Adding: 75 + 50 + 75 + 50 = 250 cm.

mcqs.q: What does perimeter mean?
options: The total length all around a figure
The length of one side only
mcqs.why: Perimeter means the total length all around the figure, found by adding all of its sides.

mcqs.q: How do we find the perimeter of a shape?
options: Add the lengths of all its sides
mcqs.why: To find the perimeter, add the lengths of all the sides of the figure one by one.

mcqs.q: A square has each side 38 cm. Which sum gives its perimeter?
mcqs.why: A square has 4 equal sides, so its perimeter is 38 + 38 + 38 + 38, which equals 152 cm.

mcqs.q: For the rectangle 6 cm by 3 cm, which sides are added to get the perimeter?
mcqs.why: A rectangle has two lengths and two widths, so all four sides 6, 3, 6 and 3 are added.

mcqs.q: For the window 75 cm by 50 cm, what is 75 + 50 + 75 + 50?

lessons.title: Picture Graphs
lessons.notes_html:
Reading a picture graph

A picture graph shows numbers with pictures. Always check what one picture stands for. In Exercise 57 (A), one egg picture represents 5 eggs: the 1st day has 8 pictures, the 2nd day 10, the 3rd day 15 and the 4th day 11. In part (B), one animal picture represents 2 animals in the zoo.

Worked example

How many eggs were sold on the 4th day?

Step 1: Count the pictures for the 4th day: 11 pictures.

Step 2: One picture represents 5 eggs.

Step 3: Multiply: 11 x 5 = 55.

Answer: 55 eggs were sold on the 4th day.

In the zoo graph, rabbits have 5 pictures, so there are 5 x 2 = 10 rabbits, the most of any animal.

Key points

  • Eggs per day: 40, 50, 75 and 55.
  • Most eggs were sold on the 3rd day.
  • Total zoo animals = 36.

lessons.title: Picture Graphs with a Scale
lessons.notes_html:
One picture can stand for many

In Exercise 57 (C), the picture graph shows vehicles passing on a road, and one picture represents 10 vehicles. This is called the scale of the graph. Cars have 5 pictures, vans 4, motor bikes 3, buses 2 and bicycles 4.

Worked example

How many buses passed on the road?

Step 1: Count the bus pictures: 2 pictures.

Step 2: One picture represents 10 vehicles.

Step 3: Multiply: 2 x 10 = 20.

Answer: 20 buses passed on the road.

Cars have the most pictures, so cars passed the most: 5 x 10 = 50 cars.

Motor bikes have 3 pictures, so 3 x 10 = 30 motor bikes passed, and bicycles have 4 pictures, so 40 bicycles passed.

Key points

  • Scale: 1 picture = 10 vehicles.
  • Cars 50, vans 40, motor bikes 30, buses 20, bicycles 40.
  • Buses passed the least.
